### 3.64 hunt-flow@23: BATT'S FIXED LOOT WORKFLOW (pre-registered 2026-10-17 11:22 ICT, the commit time 4748057, BEFORE its run; Batt 11:0x; round 3 of docs/competition.md)

**Why:** loot is still the top loser. v21's frame difference (21.8 %) and v22 (18.7 %) pick about
one drop in five; Batt picks 62 of 64. The item-sprite detector (`loot_icons`, b1289b2) was built
for v23 but **replaced by Batt before its run**. It stays in the code, unrun.

**Batt's method (his words, 11:0x):** "a FIXED WORKFLOW after every kill... no item detection, no
cursor reads":
1. take the death cell (the target's last tracked cell);
2. burst-click the death cell first, then click through the 8 cells of the 3 x 3 around it, on
   screen positions from the camera / floor model on the freshest frame;
3. no analysis and no waiting for the cursor: empty ground just steps the GM, items pick up;
4. safety only: skip a cell near a NON-target box, the pink walk guard, an NPC, a UI window; never
   outside the game frame;
5. then hunt on at once.

**Tuned from his demo (`20261016T093835-demo-human-demo`, input log + packets):**
- clicks per loot p50 1 (mean 2.38), 5-16 px from the death cell's projection;
- click interval during loot p50 0.74 s (p25-75 0.53-1.16);
- **his click -> pickup request p50 0.03 s (p90 0.27 s)**: the items lie within pickup range, so
  the server takes the item at once;
- kill -> last pickup p50 1.56 s.

**The ONE main change (`loot_fixed`, e37bfb1 + the pink fix bcb126a), on v22:**
- After the bot's "dead", `loot_plan`: the death cell twice (jitter (-6, +3) px, then (+6, -4): the
  item sprites' measured bias), then the other 8 cells once each in the server's drop-pattern order
  (SE, W, N, then the rest; `deathcell.scan_order`). That is 10 clicks.
- **0.3 s apart, bounded at 4 s.** This deviates from Batt's 0.74 s: he aims 2.38 clicks at
  items he sees, while the fixed plan clicks 10 cells blind; at 0.74 s it would take 7.4 s a kill
  against his 1.56 s. His click -> pickup request p90 of 0.27 s says 0.3 s does not cut a pickup
  short.
- Each click point is re-projected from the GM's measured position at that moment (the GM steps
  with every click).
- **Skips (safety only, no cursor read):**
  - within 30 px of any monster or NPC box (the latest detector frame; the GM's own box is not
    one);
  - within 2 cells of a known NPC cell;
  - **Batt's "pink walk guard", for loot:** > 100 NEW pink pixels within 40 px of the click point.
    NEW = not pink in the frame ~1.8 s before the death, camera-aligned by the GM's measured move
    (a Poring's corpse does not count). It is a count, not the walk guard's "any pink pixel",
    because the drops themselves are pinkish-red: an Apple's sprite holds 64 such pixels, a Red
    Herb's 33, a Creamy's wings far more;
  - on a UI window or outside the game frame.
- Every click is logged (`kind: loot, src: fixed`); every step as `loot_fixed` (clicks, skips by
  reason, seconds). Then the hunt resumes at once.

**Also logged (measurement only, no decision; 5f182f8):** the pixel SPECIES CHECK in shadow beside
every name-tag read (`species_shadow`). It skips no tag read in this version.

**v22 as the reference (3.63):** loot 34 / 182 (18.7 %), kill -> last pickup p50 7.39 s, engaged
113.6 kills / h, the bar 80.0 %, 10 walk clicks turned attack, hard bars passed.

**Run:** 60 min, round 3's seed 20270401 (the agent's round-3 start area), the same test state,
nice 10, detector on the CPU (GPU freeze), judged on the full run and on 10-min windows.

**Prediction, written before the run:**

  hour, none on a non-target;

### 3.65 hunt-flow@24: THE FIXED LOOT'S DEATH CELL (pre-registered 2026-10-17 12:29 ICT, the commit time 4ccf083, BEFORE its run; Batt's loot workflow, iterated; round 4 of docs/competition.md)

**Why: v23 put its fixed loot in the wrong place** (3.64).

  item. 2 of 5 were within 40 px (attempt 1).

  of 93 kills within 40 px; v23 attempt 1: 8 of 9). The strike aims at the body; the drops lie

  (v22) / 84 % (v21) / 91 % (Batt).

  340 drops):

  | death cell | in its 3 x 3 | within 2 cells |
  |---|---|---|
  | the cell under the last strike click | 61 % | 79 % |
  | the GM's neighbour toward that click | 63 % | 87 % |
  | **hybrid: the click's cell when beside the GM, else the neighbour** | **63 %** | **87 %** |
  | the GM's own cell | 60 % | 85 % |

**The ONE main change (`loot_death: hybrid`, 677b6fa), on v23 (+ the input fix `FrameGuard`,
f4a8ebe, which changes no decision):**

  the frame the click was aimed in (our measured position at that click). It is used when it lies
  within 1 cell of where we stand now; else the GM's neighbour in its direction.

  plus the checks), so a 4 s step gave 6-7 of its 10 clicks. The sleep is now 0.05 s (about

  not cut a pickup short.

  NPCs, a Creamy's new pink, the UI, off the frame), no cursor read, no item detection.

**Also (measurement only):** the species shadow now grabs a crop around the box, not the whole
frame (that grab delayed every tag read in v23), and counts only OTHER monster boxes as crowding
(v23's flag compared a box with itself).

### 3.66 hunt-flow@25: THE NAME TAG ONLY WHEN AMBIGUOUS (pre-registered 2026-10-17 14:02 ICT, the commit time 3b5d3a1, BEFORE its run; Batt's competition work order item 3; round 5 of docs/competition.md)

**Why:** the name-tag step costs time and fails often.
- v22: 41 % of the strike calls were refused because the tag read NOTHING (121 of 174). v23: 44
  of the 140 tag reads read nothing.
- The strike waits for the GM to stop. v22: in range -> click p50 1.55 s (260 s an hour);
  selection -> click p50 2.74 s.
- Batt clicks a monster from ~4 cells while walking (72.7 % of his walk clicks are sent while
  moving): seen -> click 1.11 s, against the bot's 3.6-7.3 s.

**The species check (`scripts/species_check.py`, feea60d), validated live in SHADOW in v23:**
- 156 tag reads in v23 attempts 1 and 2: the check was sure on 57 (37 %; offline 78 %, trained
  on JPEG recordings).
- Where the tag also read a name: 37 of 38 agreed. The one miss was the tag Lunatic vs the check
  Drops at confidence 1.0, both targets.
- 19 times the check was sure where the tag read nothing.
- No Creamy appeared in the shadow (the detector rarely boxes one); offline, zero Creamy accepts
  at the operating threshold 0.999 on the held-out session.

**The ONE main change (Batt's item 3, the NAME TAG, 05c3dff), on v24:**
1. **The tag only when ambiguous:** before the tag read, the check runs on a fresh crop of the
   target's box. When it is sure of a TARGET (Poring, Lunatic, Drops, Pupa) and no other monster
   box lies within 50 px, the tag is not read and the click goes (`species_skip`). Otherwise the
   tag is read, exactly as v24.
2. **Start while walking in:** in range while the GM WALKS (it used to wait for the stop), with no
   risk from the risk gate and a sure, uncrowded check, the strike goes now (`strike_moving`). The
   click makes the client walk in and attack, as Batt does.
- Everything else as v24 (the risk gate and its read path, the burst, the fixed loot at the
  hybrid death cell).

- the loot skips a cell with a monster box within **70 px** (was 30; 6752a24). v24's 10 loot clicks

- the loot's pink check leaves the GM's own sprite out (795f896). v24 skipped 1-3 loot cells a kill
  as "pink"; likely the GM's red hair, which stays at the screen centre while BEFORE is shifted by

- the setup helpers get the raw agent (248d182), so FrameGuard guards only the hunt's world inputs.

### 3.67 hunt-flow@26: RE-TARGET WHILE STEERING (pre-registered 2026-10-17 15:06 ICT, the commit time 5beef01, BEFORE its run; Batt's competition work order item 4; round 6 of docs/competition.md)

**Why:** the bot commits to a target and steers to it even when a cheaper one appears.
- v22's latency budget: selection -> click p50 2.74 s, 423 s an hour, the second-largest stage.
- v7's study: a unit in sight was dispatched p50 2.85 s after it was first seen, and in 19 of 32
  cases the bot was then steering to ANOTHER target, which then failed.

**The ONE main change (`retarget`, v19's code, built 2026-10-17 02:2x and never run), on v25:**
- After >= 1 s on a target, and before its engagement starts, the planner's queue[0] replaces it
  when queue[0] is valid on the freshest frame (not done, not dropped) and cheaper by >= 2 cells
  (Chebyshev to the predicted cell, +2 for a walking target). Each switch is logged
  (`retarget`).
- Everything else as v25.

**Also (a safety layer, 49e5d51), against the hard bar of v24 AND v25: `ptr_rest_ui`.**
- After every walk click and every loot step, the pointer moves to REST over the Basic
  Information window's HP bar, (110, 66).
- **Why:** both Creamy hits came from walk clicks while moving.
  - The client's own continuous attack came 0.66-0.74 s after the click, with no click of ours
    between.
  - In v24's frames, the Creamy was not within 160 px of the click point on the frame before the
    click; it flew in under the RESTING pointer.
  - Of v24's 15 walk-click attacks, all came 0.35-1.45 s after the click, mostly with no detector
    box near the click point.
  - **Hypothesis:** this client attacks a monster that comes under the resting pointer after a
    walk click. Over the UI, no monster can.
- Checked live before this run: resting there keeps the UI gate "clear" and the HP read 1.0, with
  no tooltip.
- **Measured:** walk-click attack requests per hour (v24 15, v25 13).

**v25 as the reference (3.66):** seen -> click p50 4.26 s, in range -> click p50 1.25 s, the bar 70.9 %, engaged 98.9 kills / h (sight 30 per window), loot 61.8 %, walk-click attack requests 13, HARD BARS FAILED (a walk-click Creamy).

**Run:** 60 min, round 6's seed 20270701 (bot first this round), the same test state, nice 10,
detector on the CPU (GPU freeze), judged on the full run and on 10-min windows.

**Prediction, written before the run:**
- selection -> click p50 below v25's by >= 15 %;
- seen -> click p50 <= v25's;

### 3.68 hunt-flow@27: BATTLESHIP, the belief map of hidden monsters (pre-registered 2026-10-17 16:08 ICT, the commit time 76442b0, BEFORE its run; Batt's "Battleship" idea; round 7 of docs/competition.md)

**Batt's idea (2026-10-17):**
- a grid of walkable cells; detections -> cells -> tracks with their last-seen time;
- PREDICT a random-walk spread at the species' speed, with a time cap;
- NEGATIVE EVIDENCE: a cell in view, not occluded, with no monster lowers the belief;
- PROBE the most probable cells; USE it for hidden targets, off-screen targets, identity through
  dropouts and the search bias.

**Built and validated offline first (`scripts/belief_map.py`, merged 8268666, a subagent):**
- 5 sessions, 53,302 detector frames, scored leave-one-session-out against the packets' true
  cells.
- Hidden = alive, inside the 14-cell AOI, unboxed >= 1 s.
- Spaced top-3 probes within 1 cell, the best variant (negative evidence + walk-on lead):
  66 / 54 / 26 / 19 % at 1-2 / 2-5 / 5-10 / > 10 s hidden; off screen 82 / 70 / 36 / 25 %.
- Occluder maps add -1 to +2 points: the hidden monsters are mostly detector dropouts and
  off-screen walks, not static cover. They are not used.
- Expected gain, conservative: +1.2-2.2 kills per 10 min (+6-11 %).

**The ONE main change (`belief`, wired fef14c7 + f8d2e0e), on v26:**
- The planner feeds the map from every new detector frame: our sightings' cells (with the
  selection's gates: no Creamy, no floor item, no UI) and the cells in view as negative evidence,
  each at our measured position at that frame.
- A monster unseen 1-10 s, seen at least twice, whose existence mass after the negative evidence
  is >= 0.3, and not within 2 cells of one of our kills in the last 30 s, is a GHOST.
- The best ghost's most probable reachable cell becomes the SEARCH GOAL, ahead of the heading
  search (`belief_goal`). When the detector sees the monster again, the normal engagement takes
  over.
- Batt's hover PROBE (SWORD / tag on the probable cells) is NOT in this version: the name tag
  needs ~0.5 s to show, and the probes' hit rate on screen was 57 / 49 % at 1-5 s offline. This
  version tests the walk-toward use first.
- An error in the map logs `belief_error` once and turns the map off; it never stops the run.
- **Also (a safety fix, 23a72aa):** a target is dropped after 10 s of steering with no click
  (v26's stop).

**v26 as the reference (3.67):** 39.8 min (stopped on a steering deadlock, now fixed): 129.1 kills / h (engaged 124.5), the bar 85.4 %, seen -> click p50 3.16 s, sight 30 per 10-min window, loot 55.7 %, hard bars PASSED.

**Run:** 60 min, round 7's seed 20270801 (the agent first this round), the same test state,
nice 10, detector on the CPU (GPU freeze), judged on the full run and on 10-min windows.

**Prediction, written before the run:**
- belief goals >= 20 an hour, and >= 25 % of them followed within 10 s by an engagement of a
  monster within 3 cells of the goal ("hidden kills");
- monsters in sight per 10-min window (median) >= v26's;
- engaged kills / h >= v26's;
- hard bars: zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-target hit.

**RUN 1 RESULT (2026-10-17 16:21:00, session 20261017T162100-demo-hunt-flow27, seed 20270801).
STOPPED BY ME at 28.8 min:** my live hard-bar monitor (read-only packets, never fed to the bot)
showed a Creamy hit at 28.5 min.
- **HARD BARS FAILED: one non-target hit, a Creamy, from a WALK click** (gate map+units).
  - **The cause, found and checked live:** the input log shows our pointer moving to the rest spot
    0.63 s before the client's attack request. But the recorded frame 0.8 s after the click still
    shows the client's own cursor ON the click point, with the Creamy's name tag under it.
  - Checked live at 16:5x: **one pointer jump never moves the client's drawn cursor; two motions
    do** (the "walk marker needs two motions" trait, now for the cursor itself).
  - So v26 / v27's pointer rest was INERT. The Creamy flew under the cursor left on the world,
    and the client attacked it.
  - v26's clean hard bars were luck, not the rest. 3.67's reading is corrected by this.
  - **Fixed in v28 (da581ca):** the rest goes in two motions.
- **The belief map (the main change):**
  - 1,899 `belief_goal` events, 380 distinct goals (a new ghost or a new probe cell): ~13 a
    minute;
  - 44 of the 380 (12 %) were followed within 10 s by an engagement of a target within 3 cells of
    the goal, all 44 dead;
  - at the goal time, a live monster was within 1 cell of the goal for 58 (15 %) (packets);
  - **a re-plan loop:** at a probe exactly 2 cells away, the planner re-planned the same ghost
    every 0.1 s until negative evidence dropped its mass below 0.3 (~2 s standing). Fixed for v28:
    each ghost is chased once.
- **Engagements:** 75 (all dead). The bar 56 / 74 = 75.7 % (Wilson 64.8-84.0).
- **Kills:** 141.7 / h; engaged 139.6 / h (v26 124.5). Sight 24 per 10-min window (v26 30).
- **Loot:** 52 of 109 (47.7 %); kill -> last pickup p50 4.09 s.
- **vs the prediction:**

### 3.70 hunt-flow@29: BATT'S INTERLEAVED A / B / C STRIKE TEST (pre-registered 2026-10-17 17:59 ICT, the commit time 361021b, BEFORE its run; Batt 17:3x; rounds 9+ of docs/competition.md)

**Batt's test (17:3x), following the two-motion cursor finding (3.68):**
- burst-click at once when the pointer reaches the monster, until the client's LOCK ARROW appears
  on it, without waiting for a confirmation;
- **why beyond speed:** if one pointer jump does not update the client's cursor, a click right
  after the jump may be resolved at the OLD cursor spot. That would be another cause of our misses,
  so one arm adds a second small motion.

**The lock arrow, PROVEN from pixels against packets first** (`arrowproof.py`; v24-v27, 290
bursts that ended on the arrow; our attack request on the engagement's gid within 3.5 s of the
click):
- in 257 the request came on that target; in 15 the target was already dying from an earlier
  hit; together 93.8 % mean "the target is locked";
- in 8 the request went to ANOTHER unit (2.8 %), and in 10 only a walk followed (3.4 %, a false
  arrow);
- **timing: the arrow appears BEFORE the request** (arrow - request p10 / p50 / p90 -1.04 /
  -0.36 / +0.52 s). The client locks the target at the click, walks in, then sends the request.
  So the arrow is the EARLIER stop signal;
- recall: 257 of the 350 bursts with a request ended on the arrow (73 %). The other bursts end on
  the bound (4 clicks / 3 s) or when the box is gone, as before;
- click -> our attack request p10 / p50 / p90 0.22 / 0.74 / 1.32 s.

**The ONE main change (`abc`, 578a14b), on v28 (3.69: hard bars passed for the full hour,
141.9 kills / h): three arms INTERLEAVED per engagement** (arm =
k % 3 of the engagement counter, so spawns, map area and time are matched):
- **A (confirm first):** the pointer on the target (two motions, read_tag), the client's
  confirmation, then the click. On the direct path the confirmation is the NAME TAG (it shows
  only for a unit under the pointer, and names its species); the tag cache (3 s / 60 px) counts as
  "where required". The species check does NOT skip the tag in A.
- **B (Batt):** the click at once (one pointer move + click), then the burst until the lock arrow
  (or the bound).
- **C (B + nudge):** a second small motion first (to +2 / +1 px, 0.03 s), then the click and the
  same burst.
- The burst after the first click is the same in all arms (0.6 s apart, <= 4 clicks / 3 s, ends
  on the arrow).
- **Safety: B / C only for a confident target with nothing risky near; otherwise the engagement
  falls back to A** (logged with its reason).
  - Confident = the pixel species check sure and uncrowded, or the track's tag within the cache
    rule.
  - The risk gate chose the direct path: no non-target species box, no NPC within 12 cells, no
    overlap, not under the GM.
  - No pink other than the target's own sprite within 60 px of the click (a Creamy, or another
    Poring).
- Every first click logs its planned arm, its effective arm, the fallback reason, and the pointer
  arrival time.
- Hard bars unchanged. My read-only live hard-bar monitor stays on; a non-target hit stops a run.

**Measured per arm** (`abc.py`, pooled to >= 60 engagements per effective arm, over as many runs
as it takes):
- pointer arrival -> our attack request on the target (p50 / p90);
- clicks per lock;
- landing within 5 s;
- misclicks: a strike click resolved to the ground (a walk request and no attack request
  <= 1.5 s) or to another unit (an attack request on another gid);
- non-target hits; dead share; arrival -> the target's death; the run's kills / h.

**Prediction, written before the run:**
- arrival -> attack request p50: B and C at least 0.3 s below A;
- clicks per lock: C <= B;
- misclicks (ground + other): C below B (the old-cursor hypothesis); if C == B, the hypothesis is
  not supported for strike clicks;
- landing within 5 s: B and C >= A - 5 points;
- non-target hits: zero in every arm;
- hard bars: zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-target hit.

**Run:** 60 min per run, seeds 20271001, 20271101, ... (bot only: the agent's rounds end at
round 8 to give the pooled test its hours). The same test state, nice 10, detector on the CPU
(GPU freeze).

**Amendment (written 2026-10-17 18:5x, before run 2; Batt's decisions at 18:3x):**
- **Run 2 onward runs v30 = v29 with the Battleship belief map OFF** (decision 2: as a search goal
  it does not pay). The arms are interleaved within each run, so the per-arm comparison is
  unaffected; the runs are pooled per arm. Run 1 (v29, belief on) counts too.
- **A Creamy hit is no longer a hard bar** until a Creamy-aware detector is trained (decision 3).
  It no longer stops a run or vetoes a version; it is counted and reported separately per arm.
  Hard bars stay: NPC contact, map change, unknown UI state, a hit on any other non-target.
- **The agent's rounds continue** (decision 4), alternating around the bot's runs.

**RESULT (pooled over 3 runs: v29 18:11 60 min, v30 19:26 60 min, v31 20:29 45 min; 337
engagements; every run's hard bars passed; 0 Creamy hits; `abc.py`):**

| arm (effective) | n | arrival -> click | arrival -> our attack request p50 / p90 | clicks per lock (mean) | landing <= 5 s | first click: target / other unit / ground | non-target | arrival -> kill p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (confirm first) | 194 | 0.62 s | 1.42 / 2.17 s | 1.08 | 149 / 194 = 77 % | 143 / 11 / 40 | 0 | 2.46 s |
| B (click at once) | 69 | 0.02 s | **0.79** / 1.49 s | 1.13 | 49 / 69 = 71 % | 46 / 0 / 23 | 0 | **1.79 s** |
| C (B + nudge) | 71 | 0.11 s | 0.89 / 1.77 s | 1.16 | **61 / 71 = 86 %** | 52 / 0 / 19 | 0 | 1.88 s |

- Planned arms were 111 / 111 / 112. B and C fell back to A on 42 and 41 engagements, mostly
  "species unsure" (the pixel check's coverage).
- **vs the prediction:**
  - B and C at least 0.3 s faster to the request than A: YES (0.63 and 0.53 s faster);
  - clicks per lock C <= B: NO (1.16 vs 1.13, the same within noise);
  - misclicks C below B: YES (ground first clicks 27 % vs 33 %; neither ever clicked another unit,
    A 6 %). This supports the old-cursor hypothesis, but weakly at n ~70;
  - landing B and C >= A - 5 points: C YES (86 vs 77 %), B NO (71 %, -6);
  - non-target hits: zero in every arm: YES;
  - hard bars: PASSED in all three runs.
- **Verdict:** **C** (the second small motion, then burst to the lock arrow) is as fast as B and
  lands best. It is the candidate for the next version's default strike on confident targets. A
  stays the fallback for an unsure or crowded species.

### 3.71 hunt-flow@31: THE DEATH CELL WHERE THE HIT LANDED (pre-registered 2026-10-17 20:28 ICT, the commit time 2c4d8ae, BEFORE its run; Batt's decision 1 at 18:3x; round 10 of docs/competition.md)

**Batt (18:3x):** "the LAST STRIKE CLICK is NOT the death cell (a hit monster can still walk away;
we follow and click again elsewhere). Use where the monster actually was when OUR HIT LANDED ...
or where its death animation plays. Build it from pixels ... Validate offline against packets ...
Bar: loot >= 80 %."

**Offline validation against packets** (`deathcells.py`; v24, v25, v26, v28; dead engagements;
"3 x 3" = the share of the kill's dropped items inside the 3 x 3 around the candidate; the
packets' death cell is biased by the walk model, so the drops are the reference):

| candidate death cell | exact / <= 1 cell from the death cell | drops inside its 3 x 3 | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| the last strike click (v24-v30) | 31 % / 48 % | 54 % | 476 |
| the target's box at our first hit | 61 % / 86 % | **90 %** | 83 |
| the target's box at our last hit | 61 % / 86 % | 90 % | 83 |
| the death animation (its last box) | 66 % / 87 % | 86 % | 83 |
| (packets: its cell at our hit) | 62 % / 76 % | 86 % | 476 |

- Every kill at STR 99 is ONE hit, so the first and last hit are the same moment. The hit cell
  and the death animation agree with the packets' own position at the hit (86-90 %).
- n 83: offline, a box was matched to the target near the hit frame only when it lay within
  60 px of the last strike click. The live bot has its own track of the target, so live coverage
  is higher.
- **Wandering (Batt's question, the GM immune):**
  - every kill was a single hit, so "stand and fight" cannot be observed at STR 99;
  - 19 % of the targets had started a walk between our hit and their vanish;
  - 24 % lay >= 2 cells from where our hit found them. Their walk position is the server's
    model, so that is an upper bound.

**The ONE main change (`loot_death: anim`, 531cbb8), on v30:**
- The fixed loot's 3 x 3 centres on the target's own LAST box (the hit / the death animation).
- Its foot (bottom centre, 4 px up) becomes a cell with OUR measured position at THAT frame's time
  (`pos_at_frame`), not where we stand at the loot step.
- The hybrid cell (v24) only when the track has no box.
- The A / B / C strike test keeps running inside it (3.70), and is pooled.

**v30 as the reference:** v30 run (20261017T192601-demo-hunt-flow30, seed 20271101, the full hour, hard bars passed): 105.0 kills / h (engaged 99.0), the bar 78.0 %, seen -> click p50 3.26 s, sight 25.5 per window, loot 63 / 128 (49 %), kill -> last pickup p50 3.34 s.

**Run:** 45 min (so the agent's round 10 and the day's wrap-up fit before 22:00), round 10's seed 20271201 (bot first this round), the same test state, nice 10,
detector on the CPU (GPU freeze); my live hard-bar monitor on. A Creamy hit is counted, not a
stop (Batt 18:3x).

**Prediction, written before the run:**
- loot picked / dropped >= 70 % (v28 53 %, v25 62 %; Batt's bar 80 %);
- the loot step's death cell within 1 cell of the packets' death cell for >= 70 % of kills;
- kill -> last pickup p50 <= 3.0 s;
- engaged kills / h >= v30's - 10 %;
- hard bars: zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero hit on a non-target other than a Creamy
  (Creamy hits reported apart).

**RUN 1 RESULT (2026-10-17 20:29:27-21:14:27, session 20261017T202927-demo-hunt-flow31, seed
20271201; 45 min; my live monitor on, none found):**
- **HARD BARS PASSED**; 0 Creamy hits.
- **Loot:** 48 of 82 items (58.5 %; v30 49 %, v28 53 %); kill -> last pickup p50 3.32 s. All 77
  loot steps used the hit-landed cell (`fixed_from: anim`).
- **Engagements:** 78 (77 dead). The bar 66 / 78 = 84.6 %.

  - loot >= 70 %: NO (58.5 %), but the best of the comparable fixed-loot runs after v25;

  - engaged kills / h >= v30's - 10 %: YES (98.6 vs 99.0);

### 3.73 hunt-flow@33: LOOT IS A RACE, interleaved per loot step (pre-registered 2026-10-17 22:13 ICT, the commit time b5cceb6, BEFORE its run; Batt's decision 3 on the 21:33 report)

**Batt's decision 3:**
- loot FIRST and IMMEDIATELY after a confirmed kill;
- items first inside the 3 x 3 (item_icons);
- the death cell = the target's box at our hit (v31's `anim`, kept);
- a looter that steps onto our pile is killed, then we loot;
- report items lost to looters vs picked.

**Why:** loot is 49-62 % picked, and looters take about as many of our drops as we pick (v24 +
v31 pooled, `arm_judge.py loot`: 230 items, 101 picked, 52 lost to a looter, 77 gone otherwise).

**The ONE main change (`loot_race`, interleaved by `loot_race_ab`): odd loot steps are the RACE
arm, even ones the PLAIN arm (v32's fixed 3 x 3).**
- **Items first:** one fresh grab around the death cell, `item_icons.find_items` on it (radius
  110 px; only our own pointer excluded, the configuration its offline eval measured: recall@15
  ~0.39, 0.15 false a kill). Each match is clicked FIRST at its own pixel, nearest the GM first;
  then the whole fixed 3 x 3 as before.
- **The looter chain:** during the step, a monster box that blocks a click (the 70 px unit rule)
  and stands within 2 cells of the death cell, when the species check is SURE it is a target and
  no other box crowds it, STOPS the step. The main loop engages it at once (arm C), and ITS loot
  step covers its own 3 x 3 plus our cells still unclicked. At most one chained looter per kill.
  An unsure or non-target box is skipped as before.
- Each kill logs `loot_arm` (race / plain / race_chain); the step logs `icons`, `icon_ms`,
  `looter`, `refix`.

**Base, the same in both arms (not under test):**
- v32 = arm C the default strike, `anim` death cell.
- The DEAD RULE is one rule for the whole run, set by 3.72's verdict before v33's first run:
  fast for all if 3.72's first two predictions hold (fast-arm kill -> loot start p50 <= 1.2 s,
  false deaths <= slow + 5 points), else v15's rule for all. Never two parity arms at once:
  loot steps follow engagements, so the arms would be confounded (a test pins it).
- **The loot-treadmill fix (`loot_refix`, 3.72's run log):** the minimap readout from a grab of
  its own rect (4 ms). More than 1.5 cells off the odometry -> re-anchor on it and project from
  it. More than 12 cells -> no further loot click, and the jump guard of the main loop decides.
  - It is read before each loot click and before the death cell is computed.
  - The matched item pixels use the same re-anchored position as reference.
  - *(Amended 22:24, commit 2eef8a2, before any v33 run: the first two places were added after b5cceb6.)*
- **The death-cell speed fix (`nearest_cell_frac`, amended 23:24, commit bb10f45, after attempt 1, before
  attempt 2):** the cell nearest a pixel was found by ~3 ms projections one cell at a time. That
  took ~1 s at radius 9 on EVERY kill's death cell (v31+'s `anim`, both arms, likely most of
  v32's 1.23 s fast-arm kill -> loot start), and ~0.3 s per matched item at radius 4. All cells
  are now projected in one call: the same cell (36 real-camera cases identical), 3 ms. Both arms
  get it, so the interleaved comparison stays matched; the "cost" prediction is judged on
  attempt 2+ only.

**Run log (written during the runs, before any judging):**
- **Attempt 1** (23:14:38, seed 20271501, `20261017T231438-demo-hunt-flow33`, the dead rule v15's
  for all by 3.72): stopped BY ME at 9.0 min (27 engagements, all dead, no hard bar) to apply the
  speed fix above.
  - Seen live: the readout re-anchor fired on most loot clicks (5-6 of 10), so the odometry was
    routinely > 1.5 cells off during loot.
  - The matcher found 1-2 items in some race steps; a step with matches cost 0.5-0.8 s (the
    per-icon cell search).
  - Attempt 1 is reported APART: its loot arms remain a valid interleaved comparison, but not
    for the cost prediction.

**Reference:** v32 (3.72, pooled) and v31 (3.71: loot 58.5 %).

**Runs:** two 60-min runs pooled (seeds 20271501, 20271601), the hunting fixed state restored

hard-bar monitor (`scripts/hardbar_live.py watch 33`). A Creamy hit is counted, not a stop.

### 3.74 hunt-flow@34: PACED INPUT, in alternating 10-min blocks (pre-registered 2026-10-17 23:30 ICT, the commit time 14485b0, BEFORE its run; the speed-first order, Batt 18:3x; seeds corrected 23:31, bcc49d5, before any v34 run: 3.73 owns 20271601)

**Why:** found 22:2x. `ro_agent.Agent.send()` called `wait_for_human()`, whose first step drains
the socket for a FULL 50 ms before every input.
- The backend's input log stamps each input 51-57 ms after the agent created it.
- A click is 3 sends (move, press, release), so ~150 ms of a ~0.3 s click was this wait. The
  loot step's clicks came every 0.39 s instead of the registered 0.05 s interval plus the click.
- Every pointer move (follow, nudge, rest) paid 50 ms too.
- v32's latency budget: server kill -> the bot's dead, including the 4.1 s loot step, is the top
  loser; selection -> click is second.

**The ONE main change (`send_gap_s` 0.05, `ro_agent.Agent.min_send_gap_s`):**
- The status messages already queued are read without blocking.
- A send waits only until 50 ms after the previous send, so no two inputs come closer than the
  old drain allowed. Only the dead wait after other work goes.
- A human lease is still waited out, and a mode change still stops (tested).
- `/where` and the weight clear (they TYPE) keep the default.
- **Interleaved in 10-min blocks within each run** (the input path is global, so not per
  engagement). Odd seeds start paced, even seeds start default; logged as `send_gap` events.

**Base:** v33, with its loot arm decided by 3.73's verdict before v34's first run: the race for
all if 3.73's two primary predictions hold, else the plain 3 x 3 for all. v15's dead rule for all
(3.72). The death-cell speed fix and the loot re-anchor are kept.
- *Amended 00:35, before any v34 run:* **the loot corpse fix** (`loot_corpse`) is added to the base.
  - For 2.5 s after the target's last box, a monster box within 30 px of that box (moved with the
    camera) is the target's own dying sprite, not a unit, and no longer skips a loot click.
  - Why: a loot that starts earlier lands under the corpse. v32's fast arm (1.23 s) skipped 4.0
    clicks a step, its slow arm (2.50 s) 2.48. v33 attempt 2 (0.63 s, the speed fix) skipped
    3.8 of its 10.
  - Both pacing arms get it.

**Runs:** two 60-min runs pooled (seeds 20271701 = paced first, 20271802 = default first), the
hunting fixed state restored and the weight cleared between runs, nice 10, detector on the CPU,
the live hard-bar monitor.

**Prediction, written before the runs (per arm, pooled over blocks; `arm_judge.py blocks`):**
- **Primary (mechanical, low noise):** the loot step's time p50 paced <= default - 1.0 s.
- **The input still registers:**
  - walk clicks the client followed within 1 s: paced >= default - 3 points;
  - landing within 5 s: paced >= default - 5 points;
  - loot picked / fell: paced >= default - 5 points.
- **Secondary (density-confounded, reported):** kills / h paced > default; first click -> hit
  p50 paced <= default.
- **Hard bars:** zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-Creamy non-target hit (Creamy
  counted).

### 3.75 hunt-flow@35: THE SPECIES CHECK ON THE BOX'S OWN FRAME, interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-17 23:34 ICT, the commit time 235d4c4, BEFORE its run; Batt's decision 1: cut the "species unsure" fallbacks)

**Why:** arm C, the default strike, falls back to A when the pixel species check is unsure. v32:
species unsure on 26.9-37.7 % of strikes (`arm_judge.py species`).
- The species-crop study (bca353e, 6967427; hunt-flow28-31 held out) found the cause: the box is
  ~0.6 s old, and the check cropped a NEWER frame at the old coordinates. The sprite had moved
  (p50 6 px, p90 68 px).
- On the box's own frame, gated by finding the sprite again in a fresh grab (NCC >= 0.5 within
  +-120 px): coverage 0.341 -> 0.651, wrong species 11 -> 0, Creamy accepted 1/85 -> 0/85.
- The model is not the limit (retrained on 40 sessions: the same).

**The ONE main change (`species_own`, interleaved by `species_own_ab`):**
- **Odd engagements:** `species_now(b)` classifies the box on the detected frame it came from
  (`loot1.Sampler.frame_of`, the last 4 held), and only when `species_check.recentre` finds the
  sprite again in a fresh grab. Otherwise the answer is None, i.e. read the tag (arm A).
- **Even engagements:** the fresh crop at the stale box, as v32-v34.
- It feeds `tag_gate` (species_skip), arm C's eligibility, and strike_moving.

**Base:** v34, with its pacing decided by 3.74's verdict before v35's first run: paced for the
whole run (`send_gap_ab` off) if 3.74's primary prediction and its three "still registers"
predictions hold, else the default for the whole run. 3.73's loot decision kept; v15's dead rule.

1. **Primary**, "species unsure" own <= stale - 10 points: **PASS** (15.7 vs 27.3 %, -11.6).
2. effective arm C own >= stale + 10 points: **FAIL** (67.9 vs 68.9 %).
3. landing own >= stale - 5 points: **FAIL** (63.6 vs 80.5 %, -16.9).
4. safety: **PASS**. No non-target hit and no Creamy attack request in either arm; hard bars zero.

**Consequence:** the own-frame check is NOT adopted. v36's base runs the stale-box check for ALL
engagements (`species_own` off), as v32-v34 did.

**Read: the stale crop had been a "still there" gate.**
- The fresh crop at the old box says "sure" only when the sprite is still where the box says.
  When it has moved, the crop misses, the answer is "unsure", and the strike falls back to the tag
  read.
- The own-frame check also says "sure" for a sprite that has moved: `recentre` finds it up to
  120 px away. The arm C click still goes to the OLD box (the re-centred box is not used for the
  aim).
- Effects of that:
  - "no unit under the click" 17 against 7;
  - aim error p90 56 px against 33 (run 1);
  - the target's own displaced pink sprite reads as "pink near" (22 against 2), so the
    effective C share did not rise.
- The check also costs ~100 ms (a ±120 px grab plus the NCC search) before every click.
- A next step, if the species fallbacks matter again: aim at the re-centred box, or say "sure"
  only when the re-centre shift is small. That is a new pre-registration, not this one.
- Kills / h follows the density again: run 1 had the night's densest field (15.2 / 10 min).

### 3.77 hunt-flow@36: THE LOOT RETRY, interleaved per kill (pre-registered 2026-10-18 06:08 ICT, the commit time 6c95acf, BEFORE its run)

**Why this change, and not the time-loser order:** the plan attacks the latency budget's top
loser. v34's two runs (s / h):
- dead -> next selection: 570;
- selection -> click: 570. Of this, the walk into range is ~350 and in range -> click ~225-255
  (`latency_budget.py`; v34 engagements);
- server kill -> "dead": 415.

Neither of the top two has a ready, safe single change:
- **The search is density-bound.** At 67-75 % of engagement ends, no target species stood within
  14 cells (packets).
- **In range -> click** takes ~1.1 s for moving and standstill strikes alike, so a tag read while
  walking would gain only ~20-30 s / h.
- **The species fallbacks** were 3.75's target, and its own-frame check failed on landing.

So v36 takes M1's LARGEST gap instead, the loot.
- v34 picked 66.6 % of the items at our kills, against the 80 % bar.
- Loot is a race (Batt's decision 3).

**Found (v34 run 1, `20261018T013812-demo-hunt-flow34`):** 40 of 143 loot steps skipped >= 6 of
their clicks for "a unit near".
- In 23, another live monster stood within 4 cells (packets): a correct skip, but that monster
  may walk on.
- In 15, no live monster stood within 6 cells. The recorded frames show what the detector boxed:
  - mostly the target's own dying sprite beside the GM. The corpse match (v34) missed it: the
    track's last box was > 30 px from where the sprite died, since the track is lost when the
    target overlaps the GM;
  - twice, our own hand pointer.
- A skipped click is never tried again, so a fully blocked step ends in ~0.6 s and leaves its
  items behind.

**The ONE main change (`loot_retry`, interleaved by `loot_retry_ab`; `loot_retry_of` is pure and
tested):**
- **Odd k (the retry arm):** a loot cell skipped for "a unit near" is queued ONCE more at the end
  of the step, not before `loot_retry_wait_s` (0.6 s) after its skip. By then the dying sprite
  has faded or the passer-by has moved.
- The SAME checks decide it again: a unit within 70 px, new pink, an NPC within 2 cells, the view.
  The same step cap applies (`loot_fixed_max_s` 4.5 s).
- A retry skipped again is counted apart and never queued again. Pink / NPC / view skips are never
  retried.
- **Even k:** as v35.

**Base:** v35 with 3.75's verdict applied: the STALE-box species check for all engagements
(`species_own` off, `species_own_ab` off), paced input for the whole run (3.74), the plain 3 x 3
(3.73), v15's dead rule.

**Run:** one 60-min run, seed 20272201, prt_fild08, after the held-out run. The hunting fixed state
restored and the weight cleared before, nice 10, the detector on the CPU, and the live hard-bar
monitor (`hardbar_live.py watch 36`).

### 3.78 hunt-flow@37: THE CURSOR'S SWORD at loot and moving-walk click points, interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-18 10:17 ICT, the commit time e815b95, BEFORE its runs; Batt's decision 2, option b)

**Batt (2026-10-18):** "a detector-independent check at loot and walk click points: the client's
own cursor shows the SWORD over ANY monster. Use the two-motion nudge so the cursor updates fast;
if the cursor at the click point is SWORD on a cell we didn't intend to strike, don't click there.
Measure its time cost and unknown-species hits on prt_fild06 (held-out rules) and prt_fild08."

**Why:** on prt_fild06 (3.76) the detector had no box for the species it never learned. Of the
29 non-target attack requests, 21 came from loot clicks and 5 from walk clicks: their unit checks
see only detector boxes.

**The ONE main change (`cursor_sword`, 4325f49; in hunt_flow b53f18b):**
- Before every loot click and every walk click made while the GM moves, the pointer goes to the
  click point in two motions. The client's own cursor there is read from one 64 x 64 grab per
  read, 30 ms apart, for up to 0.35 s.
- The read is a background-free colour recall against the SWORD / WALK / PICKUP references.
  - SWORD on any read: no click.
  - A drawn arrow or hand: CLEAR, then the click at the same point.
  - Nothing decided by 0.35 s: UNKNOWN, no click (fail closed).
- Strike clicks are unchanged (they intend the SWORD). Walk clicks from a standstill keep the
  robust2 gate.
- **Interleaved per engagement:** odd k = the check on, even k = off. Every loot and moving walk
  click logs its arm (`sw`), so each non-target attack request is assigned to the arm of the click
  just before it (`arm_judge.py sword`, `apart_why.py`).

**Evidence before the runs:**
- Offline, leave-one-out on the 645 references: all 26 SWORD crops read sword; no other crop read
  sword; the hand read clear 9 / 9; walk read clear 468 / 491 (the rest unknown).
- Live positive case (10:13-10:16, moves only, `calib_auto.py`, GM lines through the UI gate):
  - on a pink blob (a Poring) 9 / 10 read SWORD, first at 195-309 ms. The 10th read clear: most
    likely not a Poring (a pink drop shows the hand), but unverified: no frame was saved;
  - open ground read clear 10 / 10, first at 196-252 ms, never sword.
- Not tested before the runs: a read while the camera scrolls. The runs' own unknown share
  measures it.

**Base:** v36's adopted base.
- The loot retry is NOT in it: 3.77 run 1 FAILED; its pooled confirmation passed, but adoption is
  Batt's.
- The stale-box species check for all, paced input, the plain 3 x 3 with the corpse fix, v15's
  dead rule.
- The hunting state is rebuilt by the runner itself (`gm_state.ensure_hunting`).

**Runs:**
- **Run A: prt_fild06**, held-out rules (3.76): 60 min, seed 20272501.
  - Before it: a manual `@warp prt_fild06 175 184` and a judged screenshot there.
  - Monitor: `hardbar_live.py watch 37 --targets 1002,1063,1008 --apart 1048,1051,1080`.
- **Run B: prt_fild08**: 60 min, seed 20272601, monitor `watch 37`.
- Nice 10, the detector on the CPU, the hunting state kept between the runs.

**Prediction, written before the runs (per arm; `arm_judge.py sword`):**
- **Primary (prt_fild06, safety):** non-target attack requests answering a loot or moving walk
  click, sword arm <= 25 % of the none arm's count (and <= 4).
- **Time cost (each map):**
  - the check's ms p50 <= 300 for loot and walk;
  - loot step p50 sword <= none + 2.0 s;
  - the share of checks that end UNKNOWN <= 15 %.
- **Still hunting:** landing sword >= none - 5 points; loot picked / fell sword >= none - 10
  points (each map).
- **prt_fild08:** non-target (Creamy) attack requests from loot / walk clicks, sword <= none.

**Against the predictions:**

4. prt_fild08, Creamy attacks from loot / walk: **PASS** (0 vs 0).

**Read:**
- The client's SWORD is a real, detector-independent unit check. Where it decided, it was right:
  it cut the untrained-species attacks from loot and walk clicks five-fold on the held-out map,
  and it also caught target species standing on piles that the box check missed (Pupas).

  cursor at the new point only after ~0.35-0.4 s (the recorded frames), so most checks end
  UNKNOWN. Failing closed then costs:

  - (b) both, with the wait raised to ~0.6 s and its cost measured;

    the read waits on the walk, not on the click (but the pointer then rests on the world, which
    v26 / v28 avoided).
  Strikes (7 held-out non-target attacks) are untouched by this check: they intend a SWORD; the
  species there is the tag / pixel check's job.

**➡️ BATT'S DECISION (received 2026-10-18 13:29 ICT): option (a).** "LOOT clicks only, with the ~0.6 s
wait, and ONLY on maps with species the detector wasn't trained on (a per-map flag; on for
prt_fild06, off for prt_fild08). Walk clicks unchanged."

### 3.79 hunt-flow@38: THE AGE-WEIGHTED SEARCH HEADING, interleaved in 10-min blocks (pre-registered 2026-10-18 13:46 ICT, the commit time c46dc16, BEFORE its runs; Batt's go 13:29: "Conversion first, v38 after ... run v38 for >= 4 run-hours interleaved")

**Why (the search study, competition.md "Search study"):**
- 39 % of the bot's per-kill gap to Batt is search speed. The bot re-views ground it has already
  hunted: 43 % of its newly viewed cells were in view within the last 120 s (Batt 27 %).
- Its own kills empty that ground, since a killed mob respawns anywhere on the map. Ground seen
  <= 10 min ago yields 0.40-0.47 of never-seen ground.

**The ONE main change (staged 5a0870f; PARAMS[38]):**
- At every search re-plan, each candidate heading (keep, +-45, +-90, +-135 deg) is scored by the
  ground it would bring into the bot's own camera footprint along a 40-cell ray.
- Each cell is weighted by how long since the bot last saw it: <= 10 min 0.32, 10-20 min 0.5,
  > 20 min 0.82, never 1.0. The score is divided by walking time (a diagonal step 1.4x).
- The memory covers the whole run and is built from the bot's own measured position (no packets).
- The other arm is v22's coverage heading (`heading_goal_cov`, the current base).
- **Interleaved in 10-min CLOCK blocks within each run:** block 0 starts at the first re-plan;
  odd (block + seed) = age-weighted. Every block logs `heading_arm`.
- **Seeds alternate parity** so each arm gets block 0 (the start) in two runs, and the order
  trend cancels.

**Base:** v36's adopted base: the stale-box species check, paced input, the plain 3 x 3 loot with
the corpse fix, v15's dead rule. Also in it:
- the loot retry stays OUT (Batt's decision 1, 13:29);
- the cursor's SWORD at loot clicks only on untrained-species maps (Batt's decision 2, option a;
  0d4cacb). It is inert on prt_fild08.
So the cov arm is exactly v37 run B's none arm.

**Runs:**
- 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20272701, 20272802, 20272901, 20273002 (block 0: age, cov, age,
  cov).
- Nice 10, the detector on the CPU.
- The hunting state is rebuilt by the runner before run 1 (`gm_state.ensure_hunting`) and kept
  between the runs. The standard Lv 1 state is restored after run 4.
- A judged screenshot before each run; the monitor `hardbar_live.py watch 38` beside each run.

**What 4 run-hours can resolve (measured BEFORE the runs, 83f4d11):**
- `arm_judge.py heading` on the 10 banked full-hour prt_fild08 runs (v32-v37), with a NULL split
  (odd vs even blocks, no change).
- 95 % range of the arm difference over balanced 4-run designs:
    kills / h                        +-18 %
    sight / 10 min                   +-21 %
    encounters per no-target minute  +-18 %
    fresh ground / min               +-15 %
    re-swept within 120 s            +-7 % (relative)
- The study's expected gains (kills / h +5 to +12 %, encounters +15 %) are below what 4 hours can
  show. Only the mechanism (re-sweeping) is resolvable. So kills / h is a guard against harm
  here, not a proof of gain.

**Prediction, written before the runs (pooled over the 4 runs, `arm_judge.py heading`):**
1. **Primary (the mechanism):** the share of newly viewed cells that were in view within the last
   120 s, age <= 0.90 x cov (a >= 10 % relative drop, beyond the null's 7 %).
2. **Outcome guard:** kills / h age >= cov.
3. encounters per no-target minute, age >= cov (predicted +15 %, the null +-18 %).
4. fresh ground per minute, age >= 1.10 x cov.
5. Kills per sighting: age within +-15 % of cov (conversion should not change).
6. Landing within 5 s: age >= cov - 5 points. Reversals per minute: age <= cov + 1.0.
7. **Hard bars:** zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-Creamy non-target hit (Creamy
   counted, not a stop).

**Decision rule:**
- ADOPT the age-weighted heading into the base if 1, 2 and 7 pass.
- If 1 passes and 2 fails, it is NOT adopted: the mechanism works but did not pay in 4 hours.
  Whether to extend the test is Batt's call.
- If 1 fails, it is NOT adopted.
- 3-6 are reported and do not decide.
- Also reported:
  - per run, the block differences;
  - a read without block 0;
  - kills per sighting as the standard column.

**AMENDMENT (14:17 ICT, before run 1; LOG-ONLY, no behaviour change):**

### 3.80 hunt-flow@39: THE CONTINUOUS APPROACH, interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-18 16:37 ICT, the commit time a89d93a, BEFORE its runs; Batt's go 2026-10-18 16:2x: "Order after v38's 4 runs: v39 (continuous approach: the steer must always find a click point on the route; never stop because no route cell qualified; fix the point picker, not the gates)")

**Why (competition.md "Conversion study"):**
- The approach is the largest loss against Batt: +3.22 s per kill.
- While steering, the GM moves 37-38 % of the time (Batt 92 %).
- v38's log-only `cont_fail` (3.79, runs 1-2): 94-96 % of the steer's failed walk-click calls
  had NO candidate cell on the route; the gates refused little.
  - About half were routes <= 3 cells.
  - On the rest, the 0.6-s commanded lead point lay past every candidate the picker allowed (it
    takes only cells >= 3 ahead of it).

**The ONE main change (code fffb751 on 9c75f36; PARAMS[39]), in the POINT PICKER only:**
- `ahead_candidates(..., tail=True)`: the old order (6, 5, 7, 4, 8, 3 cells ahead of the lead
  point) first.
- Then the route's remaining cells beyond the lead's nearest cell, its END first.
- Then, when even that is empty, the route's end itself unless the lead point lies on it.
- So the picker is empty only for a one-cell route (inside the zone: the strike comes next) or
  when the commanded walk already ends at the route's last cell. Tested on 300 random routes and
  leads.
- The standstill fallback (after 1 s with no click) steps from the route point NEAREST the GM,
  not from the route's start.
- **Every gate unchanged and in its order:** view, grid, units, boxes, refused, guard; the steer's
  clear radius; the cursor gate on the standstill click. The click census is unchanged (no new
  click site).
- **Interleaved per engagement:** odd k = tail, even k = base (v38's picker). A steer always works
  toward the next engagement: the runner creates engagement k at its first attack click, and the
  engaged branch never steers. So every steer moment belongs to exactly one arm (`k_at`).

**Base:** v38's base, with the coverage heading. Only if v38 is ADOPTED by its rule, the age heading
on for all (no blocks), switched in a commit before run 1 and recorded in this run log. Also:
- the loot retry out;
- the SWORD check inert on prt_fild08.

**Runs:**
- 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20280101, 20280202, 20280303, 20280404, after v38's run 4.
- Nice 10, the detector on the CPU, the hunting state kept from v38 (the runner checks it).
- A judged screenshot before each run; `hardbar_live.py watch 39` beside each.
- After run 4: the standard Lv 1 state (end_state.py), route_previewd stopped, bot_agents [].

**What 4 run-hours can resolve (measured BEFORE the runs, 99592bd):**
- `arm_judge.py approach` on 22 no-change splits of 11 banked runs.
- 95 % range of a 4-run pooled difference (the splits share runs: a rough ruler):

    | measure | 95 % null range |
    |---|---|
    | steer moving share | -8 % .. +6 % |
    | steer s per engagement | -14 % .. +11 % |
    | approach s (steer start -> first click, mean) | -8 % .. +11 % |
    | steer start -> within 3 cells (mean) | -9 % .. +14 % |
    | landing within 5 s | -6 % .. +14 % |

- v38 run 1's parity split alone gave landing 76 % vs 54 % with nothing behind it. So only the
  pooled 4 runs decide.

**Prediction, written before the runs (pooled over the 4 runs, `arm_judge.py approach`):**
1. **Primary (the mechanism):** the GM's moving share while steering, tail >= 1.15 x base.
2. **Outcome:** the approach time (steer start -> first click, mean), tail <= 0.90 x base.
3. **Guard:** landing within 5 s, tail >= base - 5 points.
4. **Hard bars:** zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-Creamy non-target hit. A Creamy
   hit is counted, not a stop.
5. **The code ran as built (a positive check, not a result):** the tail arm's `cont_fail`
   "none" calls (`steer+tail:*:none`) <= 0.10 x the base arm's (`steer:*:none`).
6. **Reported, not deciding:**

### 3.81 hunt-flow@40: THE FALSE-DEAD FIX, interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-18 23:13 ICT, the commit time b871eff, BEFORE its runs; Batt's order 2026-10-18 16:2x and his night plan 22:2x: "v40 (false-dead fix): set its thresholds from v39's probe data, pre-register as 3.81, run 4 runs, verdict")

**Why:**
- Dead calls without a real death run at 17-31 % a run (v36-v39). Most are a target still ALIVE.
- 10-21 a run follow a burst that ended "risky": the risk gate stopped the re-clicks, then the
  slow dead rule (1.4 s since the last click, the box unseen 0.8 s) called a death.
- The cost of each: a loot step on nothing (~1-1.5 s), and the live target abandoned. Its track
  enters `done_ids` and is never dispatched again; the target comes back only under a new track
  id (v39 run 1: killed later, ~12-15 s after).

**The signal, chosen from data BEFORE this entry (no threshold tuned):**
- The probe's own candidates (3.80 amendment, v39 run 1) are too weak. After a risky burst,
  re-acquire fired on 4 / 12 alive vs 6 / 28 real; a box near the predicted pixel on 1 / 12 vs
  1 / 28.
- The death-cell fix's existing verdict (`loot1.death_of` on the track's own sightings)
  separates them. After a risky last burst, on 6 banked runs (v36 x2, v37 B, v38 x2, v39 run 1):
  - "ok": a real death 93 times, the target alive twice;
  - any other reason (gap_too_short / still_visible / unstable): 93 real, 71 alive or otherwise
    not dead.

**The ONE main change (code c64c06f; PARAMS[40], committed before run 1), at the hand-off:**
- After a RISKY last burst, the runner computes the death-cell verdict (the same inputs as the
  loot step's), after the dead rule's usual 0.4-s wait.
- **"ok" -> the dead call stands** (loot, as now).
- **Anything else -> `skipped_risky`** (Batt: "mark it 'skipped: risky' explicitly, never
  'dead'"):
  - no loot step;
  - the track is NOT added to `done_ids`, so the normal selection re-dispatches it while it is
    seen: the re-engagement, with no new click path.
- Any other last burst: unchanged.
- Interleaved per engagement: odd k = fix, even k = base.
- No new click; every gate unchanged; the click census unchanged.

**Base:**
- If v39 is ADOPTED by 3.80's rule: v39 with the tail on for every engagement
  (`steer_tail_ab` False).
- Else: v38's base (the steer's old picker).
- PARAMS[40] is committed after v39's verdict and before run 1, and recorded in this run log.
- `dead_probe` stays on (log-only).

**Runs:**
- 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20290101, 20290202, 20290303, 20290404, after v39's run 4.
- `hunt_chain.py` after the agent's judged start of run 1 (Batt: never queue an unjudged NEXT
  version).
- Nice 10, the detector on the CPU, the hunting state kept, the live hard-bar monitor beside
  each run.
- After run 4: the standard Lv 1 state (end_state.py), route_previewd stopped, bot_agents [];
  by 07:00 Monday.

**What 4 run-hours can resolve (measured BEFORE this entry, `arm_judge.py falsedead`, c707a77):**
- No-change splits (parity and pairs) of 5 banked runs (v38 x4, v39 run 1).
- Dead calls after a risky burst with the target alive, per arm: 27 vs 35 and 30 vs 32 (ratio
  0.77-0.94).
- Loot at our kills (all our kills, a skipped one included): 0.567 vs 0.585 and 0.577 vs 0.575
  (+-2 points).
- Landing within 5 s: 77.4 vs 75.7 % and 77.2 vs 75.9 %.
- Time from the last click to our kill of an alive target: 14.7 vs 12.3 s and 14.2 vs 12.2 s,
  n 17-24 an arm. A difference under ~3 s is NOT resolvable.

**Prediction, written before the runs (pooled over the 4 runs, `arm_judge.py falsedead`):**
1. **Primary (the mechanism):** dead calls after a risky last burst with the target still alive
   (packets), fix <= 0.25 x base.
2. **Guard (the loot of real kills it skips):** loot picked / dropped at OUR kills, fix >= base -
   8 points.
   - Expected about -4 to -5: ~7 real kills an arm-hour end as skipped.
3. **Guard:** landing within 5 s, fix >= base - 5 points.
4. **Hard bars:** zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-Creamy non-target hit. A Creamy hit
   is counted, not a stop.
5. **Reported, not deciding:**
   - the skipped count and how many were real kills;
   - the time from the last click to our kill of an alive target (expected shorter; not
     resolvable under ~3 s);
   - dead calls without a real death per run (the standard column);
   - the standard run row for every run;
   - kills / h against v39's runs as context only.
- The expected speed gain is SMALL: ~12 false calls an hour, each ~1-1.5 s of empty loot plus
  an earlier re-engagement. This fix is mainly about the dead calls being TRUE.

**Decision rule:**
- ADOPT if 1, 2, 3 and 4 pass.
- If 1 fails, the code did not do what it was built for: NOT adopted, reported as a fault.
- If 2 or 3 fails, it is NOT adopted: it costs more loot or landing than it frees.

### 3.83 hunt-flow@42: THE STEER'S WALK GUARD FROM THE GM'S BOX, with the route tail, interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-19 07:46 ICT, the commit time e3fc195, BEFORE its runs; Batt's decision 1, 2026-10-19 ~07:00: "WALK GUARD (the #1 cause): approve a smaller radius for STEER clicks only (the walk-in toward a chosen target): from 120 px to the GM sprite's own box + a small margin (propose the value from data). Search walk clicks and loot clicks keep the current guard. Creamy hits are counted, not a stop (my rule); report Creamy hits per hour as this change's cost. Pre-register it as its own version after v41 (one change at a time), with steer moving share as the primary (Batt 92 %)")

**Why (3.80's finding):**
- The approach is the largest loss against Batt (+3.22 s per kill): while steering, the GM moves
  35-39 % of the time (Batt 92 %).
- v39's tail picker finds a point on short routes, but those cells lie within the walk guard's
  120-px circle around the GM, which refused them 4,477 times (the base arm: 385). So the GM stood
  until the 1-s standstill fallback, and v39 changed nothing (moving share 0.370 vs 0.367).

**The margin, from data (measured before this entry; `guard_radius.py`, `guard_cells.py` in
scratch, their rules now in the code's docstring and tests):**
- Pre-guard walk clicks (hunt-flow1-15, 25 runs, no walk guard): the client turned 27 of 25,328
  walk clicks into an attack on a non-target, all Creamy. By the click's distance to the GM's
  drawn box (`GM_SPRITE_BOX`, 40 x 90 px):

    | distance to the box | clicks | Creamy attacks | per click |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | 0-10 px | 278 | 2 | 0.72 % |
    | 10-30 px | 392 | 0 | 0 % |
    | 30-40 px | 256 | 3 | 1.17 % |
    | 40-60 px | 1,215 | 0 | 0 % |
    | 60-100 px | 4,318 | 11 | 0.25 % |
    | > 100 px | 18,869 | 11 | 0.06 % |

  The counts are small; within 60 px of the box the rate is 0.36 % per click, beyond 100 px
  0.06 %.
- The camera's projection of the cells around the GM (refused / all, by ring):

    | ring (cells) | 120-px circle | box + 10 px | box + 20 px |

    | 2 | 16 / 16 | 1 / 16 | 3 / 16 |
    | 3 | 20 / 24 | 1 / 24 | 3 / 24 |
    | 4 | 5 / 32 | 0 / 32 | 1 / 32 |

- **Chosen: box + 20 px.** It still refuses every 1-cell step (a click one cell away is no
  approach) and the cells behind the sprite. It frees 13 / 16 cells at 2 and 21 / 24 at 3: the
  short routes' walk-in.

  fffb751).
- Base arm (even k): the old picker and the 120-px circle.

  unchanged everywhere. No new click site.
- **The tail is part of the fix arm because the guard alone cannot act on the old picker.** In
  v39's base arm (the old picker), the steer's failed calls were 15,909 "no candidate at all"
  against 385 refused by the guard. The near cells reach the guard only through the tail.

  clean), not adopted. So this version tests ONE hypothesis, "the GM keeps walking when both
  blocks are gone", with one new piece of code: the guard.

  guard alone, the fix arm drops `steer_tail` and the prediction below stands.

### 3.84 hunt-flow@43: THE HUNTING UI LAYOUT (Batt's three spots), with the dead-end ping-pong fix (pre-registered 2026-10-19 15:03 ICT, the commit time 23d41f5, BEFORE its runs; Batt's order ~08:4x: "Batt's UI layout change for hunting ... Do it as its own pre-registered version at a run boundary ... between v41 and the steer-guard version"; 13:3x: the combat log tab; 14:0x: "keep the order: finish the LAYOUT version (v43) now"; the ping-pong bug: "fix it ... include it in the next version's pre-registration as a fix")

**The change (code 0b9da9d + the rows fix; PARAMS[43]):**
- The client's HUNTING layout (docs/client/rathena-client.md "The hunting UI layout"): the hotkey
  bar shows one row; the menu icon panel is collapsed; the chat window shows its Battle Log tab
  (battle, EXP, item get/drop lines: Batt's category set).
- It is applied by the runner at its start through the client's own controls
  (`client_layout.ensure`, each step verified on pixels; unreadable -> stop), and the run's UI
  rectangles follow it (`route_preview.UI_WINDOWS`: the panel and three hotbar rows are no longer
  masked). The /where fallback switches to Regular Chat and back.
- The UI covers 21.0 % of the game frame in the standard layout, 13.6 % in the hunting one: the
  play area goes from 79.0 % to 86.4 %.
- On v40's runs 1-2, 9.3 % of the in-view target seconds were under the UI (ui_cover.py): hotkey
  bar 4.7 %, chat 2.9 %, Basic Info + panel 2.1 %. The hunting layout uncovers about 3.5 + 1.9 =
  5.4 % of them (the chat stays).
- **The fix (Batt: a bug, not a design change):** `dead_end_hyst_s` 10 -- a second dead end within
  10 s of the last search-heading reversal does not reverse again; the best of the 8 compass
  headings instead (test: a two-sided dead end reversed on every call before, once now). v39 run
  2's episode alone added ~47 reversals.
- Not interleaved: the layout cannot switch per engagement. Compared with the base's last 12 runs
  in the standard layout (v39 x 4, v40 x 4, v41 x 4: the same base apart from the arms each tested,
  none of them on perception).
- The Battle Log reader is LOG-ONLY (Batt's decision 3): built from run 1's recorded frames, then
  logged beside each run; it decides nothing in this version.

**Base:** v41 NOT adopted (3.82, 5974260) -> PARAMS[40] with the false-dead fix on every
engagement (`false_dead_ab` False). PARAMS[43] = that + `ui_layout` "hunt" + `dead_end_hyst_s` 10.

**Runs:** 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20320101, 20320202, 20320303, 20320404. A judged
screenshot before run 1; `hunt_chain.py` for runs 2-4 (each run's monitor bound to its pid).
After run 4: the standard layout (`client_layout.py ensure standard`), then the standard Lv 1 state.

**The ruler (`scripts/layout_judge.py`, measured BEFORE this entry on the 12 standard-layout runs;
4-run pooled vs the 12-run pool, all 495 subsets):**

| measure | 12-run pooled | 95 % range of a 4-run pool |
|---|---|---|
| bot-seen / 10 min (windowed: target lives the bot's own detector boxed) | 55.2 | -13.5 % .. +12.5 % |
| bot-seen / server-seen (both windowed; density removed) | 1.725 | -10.4 % .. +10.2 % |
| detected share (boxed lives / lives on screen) | 0.911 | -2.7 % .. +2.2 % |
| first detections in the uncovered area | 0.018 | -56 % .. +62 % |
| on screen -> detected, p50 | 0.78 s | -2.0 % .. +2.5 % |

- Why not the standard "seen / 10 min": it counts monsters the SERVER sends into our view
  (packets); a screen layout cannot change it. The bot-side measures above are its analogue.
- A ~5 % gain in raw seen per 10 min is below what 4 run-hours resolve (+-10-13 %); the detected
  share's ruler is tight enough.

**Prediction, written before the runs (v43's 4 runs pooled vs the 12-run pool):**
1. **Primary (the mechanism):** first detections in the uncovered area >= 0.05 (pooled 0.018; the
   null's top 0.029).
2. **Primary (the outcome, Batt's "monsters seen"):** the detected share >= 1.03 x the pool (0.911
   -> >= 0.938; the null's top +2.2 %).
3. **Guard:** landing within 5 s >= the pool - 8 points (the 12 runs' pooled landing, `run_row`).
4. **Hard bars:** zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-Creamy non-target hit. A Creamy hit
   is counted, not a stop.
5. **Reported, not deciding:**
   - bot-seen / 10 min and bot-seen / server-seen, with their rulers; kills per sighting; kills / h;
   - the standard run row (with Creamy hits / h) for every run;
   - dead-end reversals (heading turns of 180 within 10 s of the last) per run: expected ~0 (the
     fix), and reversals / min, also outside loot steps (Batt's new column);
   - the Battle Log reader's lines, log-only.

**Decision rule:**
- ADOPT if 1, 2, 3 and 4 pass: the hunting layout becomes the hunting fixed state.
- If 1 fails, the layout did not show the bot anything new: NOT adopted (a fault to explain).
- If 1 passes and 2 fails: the bot sees in the new area but not more overall: NOT adopted;
  reported for Batt (the layout may still be kept for the combat log, his call).
- The ping-pong fix is a bug fix: it stays in the base whatever the verdict, unless it breaks a
  hard bar.

### 3.85 hunt-flow@45: THE LOCKED-POINTER WALK (Batt's search walking), interleaved in 10-min blocks (pre-registered 2026-10-19 16:28 ICT, the commit time 8376ae6, BEFORE its runs; Batt 16:0x: "pre-register Batt's method as the search-walking change, LOCKED-POINTER WALK"; 16:2x: "Keep the locked-pointer walk (3.85) in the queue ... Report its effect on click accuracy too"; it runs after v44)

**Why:**
- 21 % of search walk clicks land more than 1 cell from the cell meant (v41's 4 runs: 1,071 of
  5,131); misplaced walk clicks start 16 % of reversals (competition.md "Pointer diagnosis").
- 93 % of search walk clicks come right after a pointer jump from >= 150 px away (a park, a read
  elsewhere); the jump itself did not raise the miss rate, but a still pointer gives what the
  jump cannot: the client's cursor shape is current on every frame, so a cursor-shape gate can
  check every click.
- Batt walks with the pointer held still in front of the GM and clicks at ~0.6 s: the camera keeps
  the GM at screen centre, so a fixed offset from centre stays "in front".

**The ONE main change (search walking only):**
- **Locked pointer:** while searching, the pointer is held still at the screen offset of the cell
  `lock_cells` ahead along the search heading, and clicks are repeated at `lock_cadence_s` 0.6 s
  (Batt's cadence; a faster setting is a later version). No rest moves while searching; the
  two-motion rule only after the pointer moves.
- **The offset by terrain:** from the client AND server walkable grid along the heading: the run
  length n of the heading's ray; `lock_cells` = min(6, n - 1) in open ground; 1-2 cells where the
  perpendicular clearance is <= 2 cells (narrow ground). Never past the ray's last walkable cell.
- **Turning:** the existing heading rules decide (keep, +-45, +-90 when blocked, a reversal only at
  a dead end, the ping-pong fix); a turn moves the pointer around the GM to the new offset (two
  motions), then it is held again.
- **CURSOR-SHAPE GATE on every click:** with the pointer still, the client's cursor shape is read
  on the newest frame before each click (cursor_gate's reader): WALK -> click; SWORD (a monster
  under it, ANY species, Creamy and untrained ones included), TALK (an NPC), NO-ENTRY -> no click:
  rotate the heading +-45 (as when blocked) or wait one beat. A detector-independent safety check.
- Targets interrupt the walk as now (the strike, arm C); after the engagement the locked walk
  resumes on the remembered heading.
- Interleaved in 10-min blocks (odd blocks = locked), as v38 and v44. The census changes (a new
  walk-click site), with targeted safety tests.

**Base:** the base v44's verdict leaves; PARAMS[45] is committed after it and before run 1.

**Runs:** 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20340101, 20340202, 20340303, 20340404; a judged
screenshot before run 1; the chain for runs 2-4.

**What 4 run-hours can resolve (measured BEFORE this entry, `locked_null.py`, 12 banked runs,
10-min block splits, 12 splits):**

| measure (search walking, per arm) | pooled base | 95 % null range | Batt |
|---|---|---|---|
| search walk clicks within 1 cell of the cell meant | 79.8 % | -2.3 .. +2.2 points | - |
| walk clicks made while the GM moves | 59 % | -4.2 .. +3.1 points | 73 % |
| mean straight run of legs starting in search | 18.5 cells | -7 % .. +14 % | 16.9 (all walking) |
| search click cadence, p50 | 0.89 s | - | ~0.6 s |

**Prediction, written before the runs (4 runs pooled, per arm):**
1. **Primary (click accuracy):** search walk clicks within 1 cell, locked >= base + 5 points.
2. **Primary (walking like Batt):** walk clicks made while the GM moves, locked >= base + 8
   points.
3. **Guard:** reversals outside loot steps per minute, locked <= 1.05 x base (the walk must not
   add turning).
4. **Guard:** kills per hour, locked >= 0.90 x base; landing within 5 s >= base - 8 points.
5. **Hard bars:** zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-Creamy non-target hit. A Creamy hit
   is counted, not a stop.
6. **Reported, not deciding:**
   - how often the cursor-shape gate refuses a click, by shape (SWORD / TALK / NO-ENTRY), and what
     it refused (packets: the unit under it, its species);
   - Creamy hits / h and unknown-species hits per arm (expected to drop);
   - reversals outside loot (Batt 4.28), mean straight run, click cadence, monsters seen / 10 min,
     kills / h.

**Decision rule:**
- ADOPT if 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 pass.
- If 1 and 2 pass but a guard fails: NOT adopted; reported.
- If the cursor-shape gate alone shows a clear Creamy drop, it may be proposed on its own (Batt's
  call), whatever the verdict.

### 3.86 hunt-flow@44: COMMIT TO A TARGET LIKE A PLAYER (the aborted-steer fix), interleaved in 10-min blocks (pre-registered 2026-10-19 16:26 ICT, the commit time 1a6e139, BEFORE its runs; Batt 16:2x: "Rank the ABORTED-STEER fix right after v42, ahead of the locked-pointer walk (it's the largest reversal source: 41 %). Design it from the data ... then commit rules like a player ... Pre-register with 'aborted steers per min' and 'reversals outside loot' as primaries")

**Why (competition.md "Pointer diagnosis"; v41's 4 runs, measured before this entry):**
- 1,019 steer spans (4.7 / min). 526 of them (52 %, 2.4 / min) end with no attack click; 443 of
  those last under 5 s (p50 2.1 s).
- 627 of 1,542 reversals (41 %, 2.90 / min) have their turning leg inside an aborted steer or
  within 2 s after it: the largest reversal source.
- What ends them: `target_lost` in 520 of 526 (the tracker no longer holds the track, or its
  newest box is > 2.0 s old, and no live track within 3 cells of its prediction carries it on).

**The data behind the design (`abort_diag.py` in scratch):**
- 198 of the 526 aborts resolve to a target unit (conversion_phases.bot_selections). At the loss,
  by packets:

    | the target at the loss | n | attacked by us within 20 s anyway |
    |---|---|---|
    | alive, on screen, inside (a detector / tracker DROPOUT) | 76 (38 %) | 30 |
    | dead or vanished (really gone) | 61 (31 %) | 9 |
    | alive, under the UI | 37 (19 %) | 14 |
    | alive, at the screen's edge (< 80 px) | 12 (6 %) | 3 |
    | off screen | 12 (6 %) | 4 |

  - In 39 of the 76 dropouts the detector still had a box on the unit at the loss: the tracker
    let it go while the monster was in plain view.
- At SELECTION (the dispatch), aborted vs engaged steers (resolved targets):

    | at selection | aborted (n 198) | engaged (n 393) |
    |---|---|---|
    | distance to the screen edge, p50 | 112 px | 162 px |
    | within 80 px of the edge | 40 % | 13 % |
    | boxed in <= 1 frame of the 1.5 s before | 49 % | 38 % |

- The other 328 aborts did not resolve to a target unit: in 139 no target unit lay within 5 cells
  of the dispatched cell (a false box, or a far target's cell error), and in 46 the nearest unit
  was a Creamy (the bot steered at a Creamy, then let it go).

**The ONE main change (two rules, one hypothesis: commit to a target as a player does):**
- **Commit late at the edge:** a target whose box's bottom centre lies within `edge_margin_px` 80
  of the screen edge (or of a UI window) is not dispatched until it has been boxed in >=
  `edge_min_frames` 3 frames. Inside the margin, as now.
- **Keep through short dropouts:** once dispatched, a lost target is kept for up to `hold_s` 1.5 s:
  the steer goes on toward its PREDICTED cell, and re-acquisition looks within `reacquire_cells`
  + 1 cell per 0.5 s held (3 -> 6). It is dropped when unseen for > `hold_s`, or when its
  prediction leaves the view or the zone. A strike always needs a fresh box (unchanged).
- Interleaved in 10-min blocks (odd blocks = the rules), within each run, as v38.
- No new click site; every gate unchanged.

**Base:** the base v42's verdict leaves (v42 runs after v43; v43's verdict sets v42's base).
PARAMS[44] is committed after v42's verdict and before run 1, and recorded in the run log.

**Runs:** 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20330101, 20330202, 20330303, 20330404; a judged
screenshot before run 1; the chain for runs 2-4; the monitor bound to each run's pid.

**What 4 run-hours can resolve (measured BEFORE this entry, `abort_null*.py`, 12 banked runs, v39
x 4 / v40 x 4 / v41 x 4):**
- Per-engagement parity splits are too noisy here (aborts come in bursts): aborted steers
  -36 % .. +34 %, reversals outside loot -24 % .. +20 %.
- 10-min block splits (4 per pool, 12 splits):

    | measure (per arm, 4 runs pooled) | pooled base | 95 % null range |
    |---|---|---|
    | aborted steers / min | 2.28 | -22 % .. +17 % |
    | reversals outside loot / min | 5.92 | -15 % .. +12 % |

**Prediction, written before the runs (4 runs pooled, per arm):**
1. **Primary:** aborted steers per minute, rules <= 0.70 x base.
2. **Primary:** reversals outside loot steps per minute, rules <= 0.85 x base.
3. **Guard:** landing within 5 s, rules >= base - 8 points.
4. **Guard:** kills per hour, rules >= 0.90 x base (a later commitment must not cost kills).
5. **Hard bars:** zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-Creamy non-target hit. A Creamy hit
   is counted, not a stop.
6. **Reported, not deciding:**
   - the abort classes above per arm (dropout / gone / under UI / edge / unresolved);
   - selections deferred by the edge rule, holds and their outcome (re-acquired / dropped / the
     target attacked), the time held;
   - seen -> click, free targets attacked <= 10 s, mean straight run, Creamy hits / h.

**Decision rule:**
- ADOPT if 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 pass.
- If 1 passes and 2 fails: fewer aborts but no fewer reversals: NOT adopted; reported.
- If 1 fails: NOT adopted.

**Run log (written during the runs):**
- **AMENDMENT (2026-10-19 18:37 ICT, the commit time 4d937b4, before any run of this version):** renumbered to
  **hunt-flow@45** (was @44). Batt's 18:0x queue change puts "EXP line = dead" (3.87, v44)
  right after v42; the run order is now v42 -> v44 (EXP-dead) -> v45 (the aborted-steer fix,
  3.86) -> v46 (the locked-pointer walk, 3.85). The base follows the previous version's verdict,
  as written; nothing else changes.
- **Build notes (2026-10-19 20:41, code 45e3974, staged and inert; before any run of this
  version; how the pre-registered rules were built):**
  - The edge rule acts wherever a target is SET: the dispatch (a deferred candidate is skipped and
    the next one in the queue may go), the opportunistic pre-emption and the retarget. "Boxed in
    >= 3 frames" = the track's boxed sightings. One `edge_deferred` event per track.
  - The hold starts at the `target_lost` moment (the tracker no longer holds the track, or its
    newest box is > 2.0 s old, and no live track within 3 cells carries it on); `hold_s` 1.5 counts
    from there. The re-acquisition radius grows 3 -> 6 cells (+1 per 0.5 s held). The target is
    dropped after 1.5 s held, or when its predicted cell's pixel leaves the view, or leaves the
    zone it was steered in.
  - While a target is held, an in-range GM does not strike (a strike needs a fresh box, as
    written): it waits for the re-acquisition or the drop.
  - Blocks: 10 min from the loop's first iteration; ODD blocks (1, 3, 5) are the rules' arm, as
    written ("odd blocks = the rules"); one `commit_arm` event per block.

### 3.87 hunt-flow@44: DEAD = THE BATTLE LOG'S EXP LINE, interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-19 18:37 ICT, the commit time 4d937b4, BEFORE its runs; Batt 18:0x: "'EXP line = dead' (Battle Log reader, validated ...): pre-register it as the version right after v42 (before v44). Dead = the EXP line for our target's engagement window (pixel fallback when no line within ~1 s). Primaries: kill -> loot start, dead calls without a real death; guards: loot picked, landing, hard bars")

**Why (competition.md "The Battle Log reader"):**
- The reader's base EXP line confirms a kill of ours: precision 0.986 and recall 0.986 on v43 runs
  1-2 (142 / 144), 0.33 s after the kill (p50; p90 0.47 s).
- The bot's own dead call comes 0.50 s (p50) but 2.58-3.51 s (p90) after the kill; and 19.5-23 %
  of its dead calls have no real death behind them.
- A faster sure "dead" starts the loot sooner: the race against looters (89 items lost to
  looters in v41's 4 runs).

**The ONE main change (the dead decision, fix arm = odd k):**
- The runner reads the Battle Log tab LIVE (battle_log.py's reader on the runner's own frames,
  10 Hz; the hunting layout shows the tab).
- **Dead = a new BASE EXP line** that first appears after our engagement's first damaging strike
  and before its end: the engagement ends "dead" at once (the loot step starts).
- **The fallback, CHECKED:** when the pixel dead rule calls dead and no EXP line appears within
  1.0 s after it, the pixel call stands only if the death-cell verdict says "ok" (v40's signal,
  here on every burst); otherwise the engagement ends "skipped_unconfirmed" (no loot step, the
  track stays selectable, as v40's skipped_risky).
  - Batt's wording was "pixel fallback when no line within ~1 s". An unchecked fallback would
    call every still-alive target dead exactly as today (no EXP line for it), so primary 2 could
    not move. The check is v40's adopted signal. This is the agent's design call, flagged to Batt
    before the runs.
- Base arm (even k): the dead rule as the base has it.
- No new click site; every gate unchanged.

it and before run 1.
