### 3.88 hunt-flow@47: THE +-135 TURN ONLY WHEN BLOCKED (reversal fix P4), interleaved in 10-min blocks (pre-registered 2026-10-19 20:07 ICT, the commit time cba01d6, BEFORE its runs; Batt ~19:5x: "Reversal fixes: P4 yes (reverse only when 0/45/90 are all blocked; matches my rule) - pre-register it in the queue after v46")

**Why (competition.md "Reversals study"):**
- Since v22 the coverage heading takes a +-135 turn whenever it scores >= 0.8 x the best heading;
  v18 took it only when 0 / 45 / 90 were all blocked.
- A 135-deg turn is a reversal by the 120-deg rule: 0.46 / min in v39 + v40. Heading turns of
  90 deg or more per search minute rose from 0.97 (v20) to 4.8 (v39 + v40).
- Search-heading-turn reversals: 1.07 / min pooled over the 12 banked runs (768).

**The ONE main change (code staged, inert; PARAMS[47]):** `cov_135_only_blocked`. The coverage
heading drops its +-135 candidates whenever any heading within +-90 runs >= min_run cells; a
+-135 is taken only when nothing within +-90 runs. The reversal at a real dead end is unchanged
(with the ping-pong fix and the pocket escape). Interleaved in 10-min blocks (odd blocks = P4).

**Base:** the base v46's verdict leaves; PARAMS[47] is committed after it and before run 1.

**Runs:** 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20360101, 20360202, 20360303, 20360404; a judged
screenshot before run 1; the chain for runs 2-4.

**What 4 run-hours can resolve (measured BEFORE this entry, `p4_null.py`, 12 banked runs, 10-min
block splits, 12 splits; reversals_study's cause of the turning leg):**

| measure (per arm, 4 runs pooled) | pooled base | 95 % null range |
|---|---|---|
| reversals at a search-heading turn (cause "search:turn") / min | 1.07 | -43 % .. +25 % |
| reversals outside loot steps / min | 5.92 | -15 % .. +12 % |

**Prediction, written before the runs:**
1. **Primary (the mechanism):** search-heading-turn reversals per minute, P4 <= 0.50 x base.
2. **Guard:** monsters seen / 10 min (windowed, packets), P4 >= 0.90 x base (the coverage heading
   exists to sweep ground; fewer turns must not cost sighting).
3. **Guard:** kills per hour, P4 >= 0.90 x base.
4. **Hard bars:** zero NPC contact, zero map change, zero non-Creamy non-target hit. A Creamy hit
   is counted, not a stop.
5. **Reported, not deciding:** reversals outside loot (Batt 4.28 / min), mean straight run,
   +-90 / +-135 turns per search minute, re-swept ground within 120 s.

**Decision rule:** ADOPT if 1, 2, 3 and 4 pass. If 1 fails: NOT adopted (a fault: the rule did not
remove the turns). If a guard fails: NOT adopted.

### 3.89 hunt-flow@48: DEAD = THE EXP LINE ALONE, THE TARGET KEPT (the loot block's first version), interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-20 09:37 ICT, the commit time, BEFORE its runs; Batt ~09:1x: "v48: dead = the EXP line alone, KEEP the target until the line comes or the sprite is really gone (no skip). Loot starts sooner (before looters) and no real kill's loot is abandoned")

**The block (Batt, 2026-10-20 ~09:1x): LOOTING EVERY DROP.** "A bot exists for repetitive work,
e.g. grinding for a rare drop for 48 hours; if the rare item falls and the bot doesn't pick it up
before it vanishes, the whole grind is wasted."
- **The block's primary is LOOT COMPLETENESS:** items picked / items dropped by our kills
  (packets, offline), with the fates split (picked, left behind, looter, expired). The target is
  Batt's 97 %.
- **Kills / h becomes a guard:** >= 0.85 x base.
- **His order:**
  1. v48 (this entry);
  2. the death-cell estimate (an offline study first);
  3. no item left behind (the HAND cursor; a loot memory);
  4. looter recovery;
  5. then v45, v46, P3, v47.

**The server's rules (the pinned rAthena e985006, pre-re; `data/kb/server.json` and the source,
read 2026-10-20 09:2x):**
- **Floor items** vanish 60 s after the drop (`flooritem_lifetime: 60000`, drops.conf;
  map.cpp:2067). Packets agree: one item fell at +352 s and vanished at +412 s.
- **The killer's loot priority is 3 s, not ~30 s** (`item_first_get_time: 3000`): only the
  top-damage player may pick it up. Then the top two for 2 s more, then the top three for 2 s
  more; after 7 s anyone may.
  - Boss and MVP drops: 10 + 10 + 2 s (`mvp_item_*_get_time`).
  - Only players are checked (pc.cpp:6209-6243). The lab has one player, so the priority never
    matters here.
- **Monster looters ignore the priority.** `mob_ai_sub_hard_lootsearch` (mob.cpp:1412) has no
  owner check.
  - They search within `loot_range: 12` cells, the OLDEST item first
    (`monster_loot_search_type: 1`).
  - A looter holds up to 10 items (`LOOTITEM_SIZE`); with `monster_loot_type: 0` it consumes the
    oldest when full.
  - **When a looter dies, every item it holds drops at its cell** (mob.cpp:3243-3248, rate
    10000). Looter recovery (step 4) can get them back.
- **A kill's drops fall at once** (`delay_battle_damage: true`).
- A client is sent the floor items within 14 cells (AREA_SIZE). Walking farther clears them from
  OUR view only: the item stays on the floor until its 60 s run out.

**The ruler: `scripts/loot_complete.py` (new, tested; a standard run_row column from now on).**
- The base is every kill of ours in the judged window: a death vanish within 1.5 s of our
  damaging act. That holds whatever the engagement made of it: dead, skipped, given up, or no
  engagement at all.
- Each kill counts all its drops, with arm_judge.item_fates' fates.
- The older run_row column, "loot picked / dropped", counted only the engagements ended "dead".
- **Positive case: Batt's demo (20261016T093835)** gives 61 / 63 = **96.8 %**: left behind 0,
  looters 2, expired 0. That is his "97 %".

| banked (4 runs each) | our kills | items | COMPLETENESS | left behind | looters | expired | kills with no loot step (their items) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v38 | 539 | 691 | 53.5 % | 31.1 % | 15.1 % | 0.3 % | 41 = 7.6 % (64) |
| v39 | 605 | 793 | 53.5 % | 28.4 % | 16.8 % | 1.3 % | 52 = 8.6 % (90) |
| v40 | 510 | 669 | 51.3 % | 30.9 % | 17.3 % | 0.4 % | 64 = 12.6 % (94) |
| v41 | 537 | 740 | 46.2 % | 37.2 % | 16.5 % | 0.1 % | 101 = 18.8 % (132) |
| v42 | 520 | 726 | 46.7 % | 33.3 % | 18.7 % | 1.2 % | 85 = 16.4 % (112) |

**Where the items go today (v42 and v44, measured before this entry):**
- **Most of the loss is on kills the bot DID loot.** Their items: picked 314 / 614 (v42) and
  233 / 417 (v44); left behind 186 and 133 (30 and 32 %); looters 105 and 50.
- Kills with no loot step hold 15 % (v42) and 11 % (v44) of all items: skipped_risky,
  skipped_unconfirmed, gave_up, plus 22-33 kills no engagement owned.
- So v48, which addresses the abandoned kills and the start time, can move completeness by a
  few points. The left-behind share is steps 2-3's.
- **v44's fix arm on this ruler:** 46.3 % against the base's 61.4 % (-15.1 points; left behind
  41.6 vs 27.4 %). Its EXP-line deaths started the loot step during the DYING SPRITE:
  - the death cell's verdict was "still_visible" in 64 of its steps, against 31 in the base;
  - pink skips were 128 against 27.

  | kill -> loot step start | v44 fix: steps / unit + pink skips / clicks per step | v44 base | v42 (both arms) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | < 0.4 s | 51 / 2.96 + 1.00 / 6.04 | 42 / 4.19 + 0.14 / 5.67 | 138 / 4.25 + 0.59 / 5.16 |
  | 0.4-0.7 s | 76 / 2.91 + 0.80 / 6.29 | 27 / 2.96 + 0.44 / 6.59 | 67 / 3.00 + 0.58 / 6.42 |
  | 0.7-1.0 s | 3 / 0.33 + 0.67 / 9.00 | 8 / 1.75 + 0.12 / 8.12 | 26 / 2.12 + 0.19 / 7.69 |
  | 1.0-1.5 s | 6 / 2.50 + 1.33 / 6.17 | 5 / 0.60 + 0.00 / 9.40 | 22 / 2.00 + 0.55 / 7.45 |
  | >= 1.5 s | 22 / 1.91 + 0.05 / 8.05 | 65 / 1.08 + 0.00 / 8.86 | 157 / 1.80 + 0.05 / 8.14 |

  A step that starts within 0.7 s of the kill loses 3-4 of its 9 cells to the dying sprite.
  "Loot starts sooner" has a floor: about 0.7-0.8 s after the kill.

**The ONE main change: the dead decision and its hand-off to loot (fix arm = odd k).**
- **Dead = a new base EXP line** after the engagement's first attack click. That is v44's reader
  and rule, with each line confirming one engagement only.
- **The loot step starts 0.5 s after the line's first frame** (`exp_loot_delay_s`; the line
  comes 0.27-0.35 s after the kill at p50), so at about 0.8 s after the kill, past the dying
  sprite (the table above).
- **A pixel dead call with no line ends NOTHING: the target is KEPT.**
  - There is no loot step and no hand-off.
  - It is not re-clicked while unseen; the client's own attack goes on.
  - If it is seen again, the normal path re-clicks it every 1.0 s.
- **The hold ends:**
  - when its line comes (dead, then the loot step as above);
  - or when the target has been unseen `exp_keep_gone_s` = 6.0 s since the engagement's OWN last
    sighting, which outlives the tracker's 2-s drop;
  - or 14 s after the first click (`exp_keep_max_s`).
  The last two end "gone_no_line": no loot step, and the track stays selectable.
  - Why 6.0 s: v44's late lines came up to 3.6 s after its 1.0-s check (4.6 s after the pixel
    call; unseen ~5.4 s if never seen again). No EXP-line death came later than 5.4 s after the
    first click (n 157).
- v44's checked fallback and v40's risky check are not on the fix arm's path.
- **Base arm (even k):** the dead rule as the base has it (pixel rule, v40's false-dead fix, the
  0.4-s wait).
- No new click site; every gate unchanged. The census and the safety tests are green on this
  build.

**Base:** v43's (the hunting layout, the ping-pong fix, v40's false-dead fix on every engagement)
+ the pocket escape. v44 was NOT adopted (3.87). PARAMS[48] = PARAMS[44] + `exp_keep` /
`exp_keep_gone_s` 6.0 / `exp_keep_max_s` 14.0 / `exp_loot_delay_s` 0.5; nothing else moves
(`test_v48_params_keep_the_target_on_the_base`).

**Runs:**
- 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20360101, 20360202, 20360303, 20360404.
- Natural spawns, the hunting layout and state applied by the runner, the weight cleared, a
  judged screenshot before each run, the hard-bar monitor bound to each runner.
- Chain-queued (`hunt_chain.py --version 48`).
- Market day: CPU only (the detector on the CPU, nice 10), nothing disk-heavy at 09:30-10:15 or
  14:00-14:45.

**The null (measured BEFORE this entry; `loot_complete.py null` over 16 banked runs v38, v39, v41,
v42 in 4-run pools x 5 k splits, parity + 4 balanced, n 20):**

| measure | the arm difference with no change between the arms |
|---|---|
| completeness, fix - base | -5.4 .. +6.3 points |
| kills with no loot step, fix - base | -5.1 .. +4.2 points |
| kill -> loot start mean (3.87's null, 12 runs v39-v41) | -26.3 % .. +15.6 % |

**Prediction, written before the runs (4 runs pooled, per arm; `arm_judge.py keepdead`, this
commit; on v44's 4 runs it gives P1 -15.1 points, P2 -2.9, P3 0.38 x, G4 -1.64 s):**
1. **P1, the block's primary:** completeness, fix - base >= **+6.5 points**.
2. **P2, Batt's "no real kill's loot is abandoned":** kills of ours with no loot step, fix - base
   <= **-5.5 points**.
3. **P3, "loot starts sooner":** kill -> loot start mean, fix <= **0.70 x** base.
4. **G4, the kills / h guard (>= 0.85 x):** engaged s per kill, fix - base <= 0.176 x the pooled
   run's s per kill.
   - Engaged s = the arm's engagements, first click -> end, loot step included; per kill of ours
     the arm owns.
   - If every engagement took the fix arm's cost, kills / h would be S / (S + d) >= 0.85.
5. **G5:** landing within 5 s, fix >= base - 8 points.
6. **G6:** hard bars zero (NPC contact, map change, non-Creamy non-target hit); a Creamy hit is
   counted, not a stop.
7. **Reported, not deciding:**
   - the fate split per arm;
   - gone_no_line, how many were real kills of ours and their items;
   - the holds;
   - the fix arm's dead_by;
   - the reader's live precision;
   - kills / h and death -> next.

**Expected size (written so the read is honest):**
- The fix arm's abandoned kills hold ~35 items of ~340 an arm; less than half of those would be
  picked. The dying-sprite delay helps both arms' comparison only where the base starts sooner.
- So P1's expected gain is about +3 .. +6 points, at or under its bar. **P1 may well miss with a
  real effect underneath**; P2 and P3 are the mechanism.

**Decision rule:**
- **ADOPT** if P1, P2, P3, G4, G5 and G6 all pass.
- **ADOPT AS THE BASE STEP** if P2, P3 and G4-G6 pass and P1 misses its bar with completeness fix
  >= base. Steps 2-4 build on the EXP-line death and the kept target; the completeness gain is
  reported as unproven.
  - This second tier is the agent's design call, flagged to Batt with this entry.
- Otherwise **NOT adopted**.

### 3.90 hunt-flow@49: LOOT BY THE HAND -- a HAND scan from a drawn standstill (Batt's step 3, first half), interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-20 13:52 ICT, the commit time, BEFORE its runs; Batt ~09:1x: "NO ITEM LEFT BEHIND: a loot step ends only when the drop area shows no HAND cursor (bounded)")

**Why (measured before this entry; docs/competition.md's loot block):**
- **Why items are left behind** (`left_behind.py`, v42 + v44, 1,196 items):
  - unclicked cells inside the step's 3 x 3: 16.1 %;
  - drops just outside it (within 1 of the true death cell): 13.3 %;
  - kills with no loot step: 11.0 %;
  - the search resuming, not the next engagement, takes the GM away (76 %).
- **Where the loot clicks land** (`left_behind.py --aim`): the step's first click is 48.5 % exact
  and 82.7 % within 1 cell; every later click 10.8 % and 52.3 %; clicks while our GM walks 3.6 %
  and 28.4 %. Each blind click walks the GM, and the next is aimed from a belief the drawn camera
  no longer matches.
- **The death cell** (`deathcell_cues.py`): no box timing beats today's last-box rule.
- **v17's HAND sweep (3.59, 2026-10-17)** picked 18.4 %: "the cursor reads mostly found NO hand
  over cells where items lay". This entry's reading: that sweep hovered cells from the same
  drifting belief, with the older cursor references. Today's reader (cursor_sword, v3 refs) has
  PICKUP recall >= 0.997 on the hand crops, <= 0.660 on every other shape. The run checks the arm
  live (below), and every hover is logged with its recalls.
- **The live positive case, measured before this entry** (v37's loot cursor reads, 2 runs on
  prt_fild06 + prt_fild08, 1,173 reads, each followed by a blind loot click; packets offline):
  - every click after a decisive read that became a pickup had read the HAND (48 of 48; 14
    more after an unknown read);
  - a HAND read was followed by a pickup request 69 of 83 times (83 %): 48 at once, and 21 after
    the client first walked to the item (0.33 s later, p50);
  - the other 14 were cut by v37's next blind click 0.27 s later, which this scan never does.

**The ONE main change: the loot step (fix arm = odd k).**
- From a DRAWN standstill each cell of the 3 x 3 around the death cell is HOVERED, in the
  server's drop order (death cell, SE, W, N, then the rest).
  - Standstill = the floor odometry (its own thread, from the frames) still for 0.15 s, waited
    at most 1.2 s.
  - The pointer reaches the cell in two motions (cursor_sword.check), with no click.
- It is clicked ONLY where the client draws its PICKUP hand (recall >= 0.90). The click is at
  the hovered point, with no further motion.
  - After a pickup the GM stands again, the position is re-anchored (v33's refix), and that cell
    is hovered again (stacked items, at most 4).
  - A hand on the 3 x 3's EDGE adds the cells beyond it at radius 2 (an edge cell 3, a corner 5;
    at most 8 extra).
  - A SWORD (a unit under the pointer) or no read is tried once more after 0.6 s. A SWORD is never
    clicked.
- The step ends when no cell can still show a hand, or at 8.0 s.
- **Base arm (even k):** the base's blind 3 x 3, unchanged.
- The one new click site is in the census (hunt_flow.py 7 -> 8, the HAND click). No other gate
  changes.

**Base:** v43's + the pocket escape, unchanged: v48 was NOT adopted (3.89, 13:5x: P3 0.742 x against
<= 0.70 x; its primary passed, +13.3 points). `PARAMS[49]` = `PARAMS[44]` without the EXP-line rule
(`exp_dead` off), plus the scan's parameters, all fixed here:
- `loot_hand` on, `loot_hand_ab` (odd k);
- `loot_hand_wait_s` 0.45 (the hover's read wait), `loot_hand_still_s` 0.15 and
  `loot_hand_still_max_s` 1.2 (the standstill);
- `loot_hand_settle_s` 0.8 (after a HAND click, before the next standstill: the drawn walk starts
  ~0.65 s late), `loot_hand_retry_s` 0.6, `loot_hand_max_s` 8.0.
- Built and merged before this entry (61fdfc4, b9e225a; merge 57238bb); `arm_judge.py handloot`
  (0e0dbc2, 6664e9b) is the judge.
- If Batt adopts v48 after all, this entry is unaffected: its arms share one base.
- ➡️ (14:58, a pointer, not an amendment) Batt adopted v48 at 14:58. By his instruction this
  entry's runs stay on the base above; the next loot versions stack on v48 + v49 (if v49 passes).

**Runs:** 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20370101, 20370202, 20370303, 20370404; as 3.89.
- **The arm checked live in run 1 at ~10 min** (offline, packets, a judgment by the agent; the
  bot never reads them). Its HAND clicks must be >= 10, and >= 90 % of them must have become a
  pickup request.
  - Otherwise the run stops: a fault (an inert or broken reader), not a result. The cause is
    recorded before anything else runs.

**The null (3.89's, measured over 16 banked runs):** completeness fix - base -5.4 .. +6.3
points.

**Prediction, written before the runs (4 runs pooled, per arm; `arm_judge.py handloot`):**
1. **P1, the block's primary:** completeness, fix - base >= **+10 points**.
2. **M2, the mechanism:** HAND clicks followed by a pickup request within 2 s and before our next
   click >= 0.90.
3. **G3, the kills / h guard (>= 0.85 x):** engaged s per kill, fix - base <= 0.176 x the pooled
   run's s per kill.
4. **G4:** landing within 5 s, fix >= base - 8 points.
5. **G5:** hard bars zero; a Creamy hit is counted, not a stop.
6. **Reported, not deciding:**
   - the fates per arm (left behind, looters);
   - hovers by what they read;
   - the scan's end (no_hand / cap);
   - extra cells;
   - loot step s;
   - kills / h;
   - the left-behind causes per arm (`left_behind.py`).

**Decision rule:** ADOPT if P1, M2, G3, G4 and G5 pass. If M2 fails, the reader is the cause: NOT
adopted, reported with the hovers' recalls. If P1 fails with M2 passing, the hand is right but
the scan misses items: NOT adopted, reported with the left-behind causes.

### 3.91 hunt-flow@50: BATT'S LOOT RULE -- stand after the EXP line and scan around the DRAWN GM, interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-20 18:30 ICT, the commit time, BEFORE its runs; Batt ~15:3x, after his 15:05 clip: "Batt's loot rule, simple and to be the DEFAULT after v49's verdict (pre-register it as the next loot version if v49 doesn't already do exactly this)"; Batt, received 18:11: "Go with v50 (my rule) as staged, case A. One change before you commit the pre-registration: match my RHYTHM")

**Batt's rule, as he gave it:**
1. Dead = the Battle Log's EXP line (v48).
2. Then STAND STILL ~500 ms: no walk click, no next engagement, no search resume.
3. During the stand, SCAN THE CELLS AROUND THE GM ON SCREEN: melee kills die next to the GM, and
   the camera keeps the GM at the screen's centre. So scan the 3x3 (then the 5x5 edge) around the
   drawn GM position, not around the believed death cell. That belief is wrong ~63 % of the
   time, and the HAND shows 1 cell off it.
4. Where the cursor shows the HAND, burst-click until it's gone and re-hover that cell. Done when
   a full scan shows no HAND.
5. Only then resume the search / next target. (Ranged attacks later: scan around the target's
   last drawn position instead.)

**Batt's change before this commit (received 18:11 ICT), verbatim:** "I burst-click while the hand
shows (no wait between clicks) and only pause when the burst ends; I loot in ~1.56 s per kill.
v49 showed slow scans let looters take more. So: inside a cell's burst, click at my demo's
interval (measure it from my input log) until the hand is gone; re-read the GM cell and settle
only between cells/passes, not after every click. Keep the 12-s cap as a bound, and add 'time
per loot step' with my 1.56 s beside it as a reported measure. Everything else as you wrote."

**His interval, measured before this entry** (`20261016T093835-demo-human-demo`: his left
presses in the input log against the server's pickup requests; offline):
- inside a kill's loot (the kill to its last pickup), presses on the SAME spot (<= 12 px):
  press-to-press p50 **0.59 s** (n 9; 0.40, 0.44, 0.51, 0.53, 0.59, 0.67, 0.72, 0.86, 1.00 s);
- presses that moved to another spot: p50 1.02 s (n 26);
- his first loot press 1.23 s after the server's kill (p50); 1.48 presses per item picked;
- kill -> the last pickup of its items p50 1.56 s (n 39; `loot_complete`, 1.563 s, his
  `flow_judge.loot_metrics` figure).
- The most items on ONE cell at once: 5 in his demo; 5, 3 and 2 in v49 runs 1b, 2 and 3.
- On the same ruler, v49's arms (4 runs, before this entry): kill -> last pickup p50 HAND 2.38 s
  vs blind 1.34 s.

**Why v49 is not already this:** v49 (3.90) differs in four ways:
- it scans around the BELIEVED death cell;
- it runs on the pre-v48 pixel dead rule;
- it waits for an odometry standstill, not a stand from the EXP line;
- it clicks once per hand, then settles.

Batt's 15:05 clip was k147 of v49's run 1b, a HAND-arm engagement:
- the pixel dead rule called it skipped_risky (still_visible), so no loot step ran;
- the item at (114, 162) was left behind.

**The premise, checked on the packets before this entry** (the GM's server cell at each kill of
ours against its items' cells):

| sessions | items | within the 3 x 3 around the GM | within the 5 x 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| v48 runs 1-4 | 531 | 54.1-66.9 % | 82.5-92.3 % |
| v49 run 1b | 251 | 62.9 % | 93.2 % |
| Batt's demo | 63 | 71.4 % | 90.5 % |

- The kills' death cells against the GM: 1 cell away ~60 %, 2 cells away ~12 %, 3+ ~20 %.
- So the 5 x 5's edge adds ~25-30 points over the 3 x 3 alone.
- Also measured before this entry, on v49 run 1b:
  - a looter we kill drops our items again: 82 of its 251 items were such re-drops, and only 24
    were picked, mostly in piles of 5-11 items;
  - a pile needs the burst and the repeated passes.

**The ONE main change: the loot step (fix arm = odd k), `loot_gm_steps`:**
- **The stand.** Nothing is sent until `loot_gm_stand_s` 0.5 s after the EXP line's first frame
  (v48's `exp_loot_delay_s` already waits there). The loot step runs inside the main loop's
  hand-off, so no walk click, no engagement and no search happen until it ends.
- **The reference.** At a drawn standstill (the floor odometry still 0.15 s, waited at most 1.2 s)
  the GM's own cell is read from the client's position readout; the odometry is re-anchored on
  it.
  - Every hover pixel is projected from that cell. So each cell's pixel is exact RELATIVE TO THE
    DRAWN GM: the camera keeps it at the screen's centre, standing on a cell centre.
  - The readout only names the cells.
- **The cells.** The GM's own cell, the 3 x 3, then the 5 x 5's edge (25 in all). The believed
  death cell only ORDERS each ring (nearest first); it is never the centre.
- **Each cell** is hovered (two motions, no click). It is clicked only where the client draws its
  PICKUP hand (cursor_sword pickup recall >= 0.90).
  - **The burst, in Batt's rhythm:** the next click comes `loot_gm_burst_gap_s` **0.59 s** after
    the last (his interval), only after a FRESH read of the same pixel shows the hand again.
    - The read starts `loot_gm_read_lead_s` 0.2 s early (a decisive read takes ~0.18 s), so
      the click lands on the interval.
    - No settle, no standstill and no GM re-read between the clicks of a burst.
    - It ends when a read shows no hand, after `loot_gm_burst_max` **6** clicks, or at the
      step's 12-s cap.
    - 6, not "no limit": it covers the largest pile measured on one cell (5) and still bounds
      the give-up guard below.
  - **Only when the burst ends:** `loot_gm_settle_s` 0.8 s (the server's answer and the display
    lag), a drawn standstill, then the GM's cell is read again for the next cells (Batt: "re-read
    the GM cell and settle only between cells/passes").
  - A SWORD (a unit under the pointer) is never clicked. An unread cell is tried once more at
    the pass's end.
  - **A bound on a hand that never goes:** a cell whose hand stays through the WHOLE burst
    (6 clicks) while the GM's cell, read after the burst, never changed is given up for the
    step.
    - v49 run 1b k129: 6 accepted HAND clicks on one item 2 cells away sent no request at all;
      the cause is not proven (a short client stall is the best reading).
    - A pickup within 2 cells needs no walk, and a stack keeps its hand, so only after the
      whole burst.
- **The end.** A pass that found a hand is followed by another pass around the GM's cell then.
  The step ends when a full pass shows no hand, after `loot_gm_passes` 3, or at `loot_gm_max_s`
  12 s. Only then does the hunt resume.
- **Base arm (even k):** the base's loot step, unchanged (below).
- The new click site is in the census (hunt_flow.py 8 -> 9). No other gate changes.

**Base:** v48, ADOPTED by Batt (2026-10-20, received 14:58 ICT, overriding 3.89's rule), now on
EVERY engagement: the base EXP line alone ends an engagement dead, the target is kept until it
comes (`exp_keep`), and the loot step starts `exp_loot_delay_s` 0.5 s after the line's first
frame; with v43's layout and the pocket escape. v49 NOT adopted (3.90's verdict, 18:2x: P1
+8.6 points against +10, M2 0.871, G3 +4.80 s): the base arm's loot step is the blind 3 x 3 as
before.
- `PARAMS[50] = {**PARAMS[48], "exp_dead_ab": False}` + the `loot_gm*` keys (and
  `loot_hand_still_s` 0.15, the drawn standstill's quiet time, as v49's). Nothing else moves
  (`test_v50_params_batts_loot_rule_on_v48`; the rhythm: `test_batts_loot_rule_bursts_in_his_rhythm`).
- Built on `feat/loot-memory` (30ae305), merged in b853669; the judges in 3f23b88.
- Unlike 3.89's runs, BOTH arms now die by the EXP line, so the arms differ only in the loot
  step.

**Runs:** 4 x 60 min on prt_fild08, seeds 20380101, 20380202, 20380303, 20380404; as 3.89.

### 3.92 hunt-flow@51: ONE PASS -- each cell around the drawn GM hovered once, a HAND burst-clicked until gone, then resume; interleaved per engagement (pre-registered 2026-10-20 22:44 ICT, the commit time, BEFORE its runs; Batt's overnight order, received 2026-10-20 21:24 ICT: "The next loot version is chosen FROM DATA ... If pass >= 2 adds little (your call, state the numbers), the next version is ONE PASS: hover each cell once, burst-click any HAND until it's gone (re-hover only that cell), then resume. Otherwise run B (v51) as built.")

**The data, measured before this entry (3.91's four runs, `lc/pass2_value.py`, offline):**
| run | steps | with a later pass | HAND cells first seen in pass >= 2 | items picked there | later passes' time / all step time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 47 | 31 | 0 | 0 | 120.2 / 487.0 s |
| 2 | 37 | 26 | 0 | 0 | 92.0 / 402.6 s |
| 3 | 30 | 20 | 0 | 0 | 65.4 / 308.5 s |
| 4 | 52 | 32 | 1 | 1 | 120.1 / 533.8 s |
| pooled | 166 | 109 | **1** | **1** | **397.7 / 1731.8 s (23 %)**, 1925 hovers |
- **The call:** pass >= 2 added ONE item in 109 later passes (~0.6 % of the 179 items the rule picked) for 23 % of its step time, ~3.6 s per step that ran one. That is little: ONE PASS.

**Why not B:** B (option B, built d3e3c78 on `feat/gm-pass2`) narrows a later pass to the HAND
cells and their neighbours. With no new item ever found in a later pass, its later pass is still
pure cost.
- ONE PASS removes that cost whole.
- B stays on its branch, unmerged.

**The ONE main change (fix arm = odd k, `loot_gm_one_pass` / `loot_gm_one_pass_ab`, `gm_passes`;
built 3d9272c on `feat/gm-one-pass`):**
- The scan around the drawn GM runs ONE pass: its own cell, the 3 x 3, the 5 x 5's edge, each
  hovered once.
- A HAND is burst-clicked in Batt's rhythm (0.59 s), re-hovering only that cell, until the hand
  is gone.
- Then the step ends (`end` "one_pass" when it found a hand, "no_hand" when not) and the hunt
  resumes.
- **Base arm (even k):** v50's rule as adopted, up to 3 passes.
- Everything else as v50:
  - the stand;
  - the readout reference;
  - HAND-only clicks;
  - the settle and the GM re-read between cells;
  - the give-up guard;
  - the 12-s cap.
- No new click site.

**Base:** v50 = Batt's loot rule on EVERY engagement (`loot_gm_ab` off), ADOPTED by Batt's decision at
3.91's verdict (P1, P2, M3, G5 passed; G4 failed and was waived by him); with v48 (the EXP line,
the kept target), v43's layout and the pocket escape. `PARAMS[51] = {**PARAMS[50], "loot_gm_ab":
False, "loot_gm_one_pass": True, "loot_gm_one_pass_ab": True}`; nothing else moves
(`test_v51_params_one_pass_on_v50`). Merged in 6155a7d.
- Unlike 3.91, BOTH arms scan around the GM, so the arms differ only in the later passes.
- Option B (`feat/gm-pass2`, d3e3c78) and the map zones (`feat/map-zones`, 3ce8c49) are NOT in

### 3.93 hunt-flow@52: MAP ZONES -- prt_fild08's zones file (C1 + C3 no-cross lines) on WHOLE runs, compared run-level with v51's runs (pre-registered 2026-10-21 09:27 ICT, the commit time, BEFORE its runs; Batt 2026-10-21, decision 1 on the overnight loot report: "Map zones: I DELEGATE the zone authoring to you ... Then merge feat/map-zones, load it, and pre-register a version: primary = time inside C1 per run-hour; guards = kills/h, loot completeness, hard bars"; Batt's day order, received ~09:1x: "Zones apply to whole runs (no per-engagement arms), so compare run-level against the v51 base runs with density reported beside it. Primary = time inside C1 per run-hour (should be ~0); guards = kills/h, loot completeness, hard bars. 3-4 runs as time allows.")

**The ONE main change: `"map_zones": True`** (PARAMS[52]; the first version that loads the zones).
- The runner loads `config/map_zones/prt_fild08.yaml` (13e497d, sha256 ~~56e5230b...~~ -- the
  `map_zones` event at each run's start records the exact sha256). Batt delegated its authoring
  in his decision 1, and the file records the delegation.
  - ➡️ **CORRECTION 09:31 (a wrong hash, not a design change):** 56e5230b was the file's hash
    before its two notes were edited. The committed file (13e497d) is **ce9f99d2...**, and run
    1's `map_zones` event (09:30) says the same. The lines and their points are unchanged.
    The proof re-run on ce9f99d2 at 09:31 is identical, item for item; the NAS JSON was replaced
    with it.
- Its lines:
  - `c1-door` (322,88)-(318,91) seals the south-east room C1;
  - `c3-door` (50,36)-(46,36) splits the island C3 (unreachable from the field anyway).
- The enforcement merged from `feat/map-zones` (0684d2c, 09:09):
  - walk clicks, attack clicks, the burst's re-clicks and every loot path refuse a click whose
    client walk crosses a line;
  - routes plan on the grid without the line cells.
- Added with the file (13e497d):
  - **a room a line seals leaves the search area and the route grid** (`map_zones.sealed_off`);
  - a monster there is seen, never engaged (`target_dropped`, zone `target_sealed`).

**The offline proof** (`python3 scripts/map_zones.py prove prt_fild08`, 09:17; NAS
`/mnt/poring-lab-datasets/map-zones/prt_fild08/PROOF.md` and the before / after images there):
- **C1 is cut off whole:** 2391 cells, x 313-381 / y 66-148, on client ∩ server walkability AND
  on the runner's stand grid, with and without rAthena's no-corner-cutting rule.
- **0 cells newly unreachable elsewhere**, under both rules.
- **200 / 200 sampled clicks from outside into C1 are refused** by the click gate (`walk_why`).
  10 / 200 clicks between two outside cells near C1 are refused too: an over-reach, not a leak.
- **The search area:** 87867 -> 85491 cells.
- **Spawn cells lost:** 2479 of the server's 89999 (2.76 %); C1 alone holds 2.66 %, about 3.7 of
  prt_fild08's 140 whole-map-random monsters.
- **CORRECTION to the candidate list:** C3 is an ISLAND (413 cells, no walkable link to the
  field). Its "door" is the neck between its halves, so its line cuts 88 cells nobody could reach.

**Base:** v51 ADOPTED (3.92): Batt's loot rule with ONE pass on every engagement
(`"loot_gm_one_pass_ab": False`).
- Comparison: v51's 4 runs (3.92: T224434, T234607, T004744, T014926), run-level.
- **Confound, named before the runs:** v51's even-k kills scanned up to 3 passes; v52 scans one
  pass on every kill.
  - 3.92 measured the step at 7.72 vs 10.11 s, about 1.2 s saved per kill on the half that changes.
  - That is about +3 % kills / h, within the guards' slack.

**Runs:** 60 min each on prt_fild08, seeds 20400101, 20400202, 20400303, 20400404, in that
order.
- 3-4 runs as time allows, one per client block. They alternate with the orcsdun01 collection
  blocks (Batt ~09:3x: "Finish the current zone-version run, then a warp-and-watch collection
  block ... then the next hunting run ... keep each hunting version's runs whole").
- Each run is launched with `hunt_chain.py --version 52 --seeds <one seed>` after a judged
  screenshot.

**The instrument for the primary:** `scripts/map_zone_candidates.py --sessions <the runs>`.
- It measures the GM's packet cells at 1 s steps inside C1's regions: the same tool and regions as
  the 18.1-h baseline and v51's update (03:17).
- Its positive case: v51 run 4 measured 1375 s inside.

**Predictions (pooled over the runs; an interim after each, the verdict after >= 3 runs):**
1. **P1, the change's purpose:** time inside C1 <= 30 s per run-hour, and no single stay
   > 60 s.
   - v51: 374.1 s / run-h (runs: 150, 0, 0, 1375 s). v43+: 310.7.
   - The margin covers the instrument's 1-s steps on C1's door cells outside the line.
2. **G1, kills / h:** pooled >= 81.2 (0.85 x v51's 95.5).
   - If it fails while the monsters seen per 10 min (windowed, the same ruler) are < 20.7
     (0.85 x v51's 24.4), the density-normalised figure decides instead: kills / h per seen /
     10 min >= 3.33 (0.85 x v51's 3.91).
3. **G2, loot completeness (gross, `loot_complete.py`):** pooled >= 73.4 % (v51's 79.4 - 6
   points, the 3.89 null's edge). Net reported.
4. **G3, hard bars:** 0. A Creamy hit is counted apart, not a stop.
5. **Reported, not deciding:**
   - the standard columns: kills / h, seen / 10 min, landing, gross and net completeness, left
     behind / looters / expired, kill -> last pickup (Batt 1.56 s), loot step time, HAND-click
     precision;
   - time inside C2;
   - the zone refusals by kind (walk / strike / target / loot) and the `target_sealed` drops;
   - any `zone_exit`;
   - kills / min inside vs outside C1.
- **A fault, not a result:** any stay > 60 s inside C1 means a click got past the gate. The run's
  events are read before the next run starts.

**Decision rule:**
- ADOPT the zones into the base if P1, G1, G2 and G3 pass over >= 3 runs.
- If P1 passes and a guard fails, NOT adopted: report to Batt with the runs' split (searching /
  steering / looting) and density.
- If P1 fails, the gate leaked: a fault, investigated before any further run.

  - The click: the STRIKE on track 113 (a Poring, dispatched at 173,357; the GM at ~171,360),
    branch "direct", `risk []`, `pred_cell [172, 361]`, `aim_src focus:105`. The click went to
    pixel **(734, 17.5), the top edge of the game region**. That is where the NPC's sprite had

  - The cause is in the STRIKE, not in v54's change (the loot step): it is in BOTH arms and in
    every version since the focus aim (v16):

### 3.96 crusader-survival@1: the Crusader's survival skills on prt_fild08, immunity OFF (pre-registered 2026-10-21 18:03 ICT, the commit time of 3.96's first commit, BEFORE they are built or run; Batt 2026-10-21 ~16:1x: "SURVIVAL SKILLS (build + test on prt_fild08 with immunity OFF before the dungeon; pre-register each): HP read from Basic Info (pixel), potion on a hotkey below a threshold, Fly Wing escape below a lower threshold or when more than N monsters are on us; Auto Guard re-cast on expiry; Endure when mobbed (optional). DEATH = stop the run, record the cause (a result, not a hard bar); the respawn dialog stays for the UI gate's known step only. Measure: deaths per hour, HP min, potions used, escapes." and ~16:4x: "Moving HP Recovery matters: I want to see whether HP regen keeps up while the bot walks and fights continuously.")

**The character:** `Crus4b7e2`, built and verified (docs/planning/crusader-orcsdun01.md 2b):
- MaxHP 5260, FLEE 122, hard DEF 31;
- F1 White Potion, F2 Fly Wing, F3 Auto Guard (cast level 10), F4 Endure;
- immunity OFF (never turned on for this character).

**What the rules may read (pixels in, keys out):**
- the HP bar on Basic Info (`gm_vitals.hp_fraction`);
- its rate of fall over the last 2 s (from the same reads);
- the death dialog's signature (`dead_game_option`);
- Auto Guard's status icon (a template cut live from the first cast);
- the clock since our own cast.

The orcsdun01 species are unknown to today's detector, so **no rule counts attackers from boxes**.
Batt's "more than N monsters on us" is carried by the HP's RATE of fall: a rate is what N
attackers produce (crusader-orcsdun01-facts.md: 3 Orc Zombies ~24 HP/s, 3 OZ + 2 Orc Skeletons
~104, + a Drainliar ~163, 8 around us ~249).

**The rules (one module, `scripts/survive.py`, built after this; thresholds fixed HERE):**
- **S2 potion:** HP < **60 %** -> F1. Then no second F1 until the bar has risen or 0.7 s have
  passed, at most 3 in 2 s.
- **S3 escape:** HP < **25 %**, or HP falling faster than **200 HP/s** over the last 2 s (~ a
  4-5-orc pack) -> F2 (Fly Wing). At most once per 3 s.
- **S4 Auto Guard:** F3 when its icon is absent, or 290 s after our last cast (duration 300 s,
  `skill_db.yml` CR_AUTOGUARD Duration1; SP 30 at level 10).
- **S5 Endure (optional):** F4 when HP falls faster than 100 HP/s and Endure is not active
  (37 s at level 10, cooldown 10 s, SP 10).
- **S6 death:** the dialog's signature -> the runner STOPS. It records the cause: the last 10 s
  of HP reads, the spawned pack and the time. The dialog is closed ONLY by the UI gate's known
  step (its second button), and `@alive` follows in the end-state restore. A death is a RESULT,
  not a hard bar.

**AMENDMENT 1 (2026-10-21 18:4x, BEFORE the first trial; judged frames pre-survival.jpg and
survival-stand-268-107.jpg):** the stand moves from 170,375 to **268,107** (detector_check's
prt_fild08 scene). The judged frame at 170,375 showed the castle gate's warp swirl under the
character and an NPC 2-3 cells away: a pack fighting there risks the hard bars (map change, NPC
contact). 268,107 is open field. Nothing else changes.

**The test bed (prt_fild08, ~~the bench's outdoor stand 170,375~~ 268,107 by amendment 1; the
Crusader stands still and does not attack: the detector cannot target orcs):**
- Each TRIAL spawns a pack beside the Crusader with `@monster` (crusader.gm_line, job check):
  - pack C = 3 Orc Zombie 1153 + 2 Orc Skeleton 1152;
  - pack E = C + 1 Drainliar 1111.
- A trial runs 180 s, or until an escape or a death. Then `@killmonster2` (no drops), `@heal`,
  and a judged frame before the next trial.

| trial set | rules on | packs x trials | what it proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| T-S2 | S1 + S2 + S4 + S6 (no Fly Wing) | C x 3, E x 2 | potions hold a pack |
| T-S3 | S1 + S3 + S6 (no potions) | C x 3, E x 2 | the escape fires before death |
| T-S6 | S1 + S6 only (no keys) | C x 1 | the death stop (the positive case) |

- HP 0: a death.

**Pre-registered bars:**
1. **S1, the HP read:** on every read with true HP < 100 %, the error is within **5 % of MaxHP**
   on >= 95 % of reads (n >= 200). The read must NOT over-read by more than 5 % on >= 99 % (an
   over-read hides danger). The packet -> frame offset is the measured one (labels 3b 1d), else

   at the escape is >= 10 % of max in >= 4 of 5.

5. **S6, the death stop:** in T-S6 the runner stops within 2 s of the server's HP 0, sends

   per minute, regen per minute moving vs still (Moving HP Recovery).

### 3.96d crusader-survival@1d: S4b2 -- Auto Guard's re-cast blind-proof and remembered across trials (pre-registered 2026-10-21 19:48 ICT, the commit time of 3.96d's first commit, BEFORE S4b2 is built or run)

**What happened to S4b (3.96c's chain):** S4b FAILS its bar (0 toggles-off).
- f1: a real cast, uptime 98.75 %.
- **f2: a toggle-off.** The icon read absent from 52 s while f1's cast was still active, and the
  press cost no SP. S4b's 300-s guard only knew casts of ITS OWN process, and f1's cast was in
  another one.
- f3: a real cast, uptime 98.8 %. It held only because the cast was its own: the icon read absent
  for 23 s (71.5-94.2 s) and again from 107 s while Auto Guard was active.
- **e1: a toggle-off** at 10 s.
- **Why the icon "vanished": BLIND.** Frames grabbed beside e1 (read-only, `crusader/agdiag/`,
  155 of 162 "absent"): the game area turns BLACK except the minimap, and the status icons go
  with it (Drainliar's and Familiar's Blind). Frame 43 shows the normal scene with no icon: e1
  had already toggled it off.

**S4b2, the rule (one change set):**
1. **Dark screen = UNKNOWN, never "absent".** When >= 80 % of the game area's open-field box
   (client 300-1100 x 150-550) reads near-black (grey < 25), the icon read is None, and no S4 press
   is made on it.
2. **The last cast is REMEMBERED per character:** `data/crusader/ag_state.json`, holding our
   last F3 cast as CLOCK_MONOTONIC (system-wide, so comparable across processes). It is loaded at
   each trial's start, and F3 waits 300 s from it.
3. If no cast is known but the icon is seen present, the cast is assumed to have happened just
   before the first sighting (the conservative side).
4. Otherwise as S4b: absent on every check for >= 1 s, then F3.

**Trials (T-S4, the stand 268,107, rules S1b + S2 + S4b2 + S6b; pack E has the Drainliar that
casts Blind):**
- T-S4 a: pack E, **330 s**: Auto Guard must EXPIRE mid-trial and be re-cast (the re-cast's
  positive case).
- T-S4 b: pack E, 180 s, started right after a, so a's cast carries over (the persistence's
  positive case).

**Bars:** 0 toggles-off (every F3 press has its 30-SP drop); at least one re-cast in T-S4 a after
the 300 s; uptime >= 90 % over both trials. Blind periods are reported (dark reads / all reads).

**Run log (chain 3, 20:07-20:17; S4b2 = e827c75; judged at the 120-ms offset; SP from the
packets):**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-S4 a (20:07) | 330 | 2892 (55.0 %) | 20 | 0 | 0 | 2 / 2 (at 1.5 s; the RE-CAST at 301.8 s) | 452 / 94 / 0 | 99.45 % |
| T-S4 b (20:13) | 180 | 3032 (57.6 %) | 11 | 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 (a's re-cast carried over; it expired 42.9 s after b's last read) | 226 / 72 / 0 | 100 % |

- **S4b2: PASS.**
  - 0 toggles-off: every F3 press had its 30-SP drop.
  - The re-cast came after the 300 s in T-S4 a (301.8 s).
  - Uptime over both trials **99.65 %** (bar >= 90 %).
- **What held it was the REMEMBERED cast (rule 2), not the dark rule (rule 1).** No check read a
  dark screen in either trial. Yet the icon read ABSENT while Auto Guard was active on 94 + 72
  checks: in a, two ~23-s stretches (21-44 s and 220-242 s); in b, 72 checks. S4b would have
  toggled it off in b at the first 1-s absence.
  - The absences are NOT explained: no dark frame, and no frames were saved by the runner.
  - Open, for the dungeon: grab frames whenever the icon reads absent while a cast is remembered
    (a diagnostic capture, unscored), to find what hides or moves it. Candidates: another status
    icon pushing it down the column outside AG_X = 1230-1235, or a Blind that leaves the centre
    lit (the 80 % rule then never trips).
  - Until that is known, the guard's safety rests on `data/crusader/ag_state.json` being written
    on every cast. It is per host and per character, and a cast by hand (Batt) is not recorded,
    so the rule-3 assumption covers only a cast SEEN on.

### 3.96e crusader-survival@1e: S3's HP path (T-S3h) after the rate trigger pre-empted it (pre-registered 2026-10-21 19:54 ICT, the commit time of 3.96e's first commit, BEFORE T-S3h runs; Batt ~19:3x: "Make sure the remaining trials reach their thresholds")

**What happened (3.96c's T-S3, packs C):** every escape so far came from the RATE trigger, not the
HP one.
- c1: 282 HP/s at 71 % HP;
- c2: 210 HP/s at 91 % HP, ~3 s in;
- c3: the chain was stopped after it.

A 5-orc pack's opening burst alone crosses 200 HP/s. So S3's HP path (< 25 %) is never reached,
and the rate trigger spends a Fly Wing at 71-91 % HP. That is a finding for the dungeon (a
premature escape costs a wing and the pack's EXP). Any change to the 200 HP/s threshold or its
window is a NEW pre-registration (Batt's call, proposed in the report).

**T-S3h (this amendment):**
- rules S1b + S3h + S6b, where S3h = S3 with the rate trigger OFF: F2 only when HP < 25 %;
- pack C, 3 trials, 180 s each; no potions.
- Pack C killed the standing Crusader in ~100 s (T-S6 t1), so 25 % is reached.

**Bars (3.96's S3, unchanged):** the Fly Wing before death in >= 2 of 3 (scaled from 4 of 5); true
HP at the escape >= 10 % in >= 2 of 3. S3's verdict pools T-S3 (the rate path) and T-S3h (the HP
path), each path reported apart.

**Run log (chain 3, 20:01-20:07; the stand 268,107; judged at the 120-ms offset):**

| trial | HP min (true) | read at the F2 press | potions | escapes | deaths | true HP at the escape |

| T-S3h h1 (20:01) | 1284 (24.4 %) | 24 % | 0 | 1 | 0 | 24.4 % |

| T-S3h h3 (20:05) | 1297 (24.7 %) | 24 % | 0 | 1 | 0 | 24.7 % |

  3 / 3). Each F2 came on the FIRST read below 25 %: rate 80-116 HP/s at the time, so the rate
  trigger would not have fired.
- **S3 pooled (3.96's bar, scaled):** T-S3 c1-c3 (the rate path) 3 / 3 + T-S3h 3 / 3 = **6 / 6
  before death, 6 / 6 at >= 10 %** -> **PASS**.

### 3.96f crusader-regen@1: HP regen while standing, walking and fighting, with Moving HP Recovery (pre-registered 2026-10-21 21:17 ICT, the commit time of 3.96f's first commit, BEFORE it is built or run; Batt 2026-10-21 ~16:4x: "Moving HP Recovery matters: I want to see whether HP regen keeps up while the bot walks and fights continuously", and again 21:1x: "report HP regen while walking/fighting with Moving HP Recovery")

**What the pinned source predicts** (status.cpp `status_natural_heal` :15444-15560; e985006):
- Natural HP regen ticks every `natural_healhp_interval` (6 s) by `1 + VIT/5 + MaxHP/200` (= 33 for
  this Crusader). It is sent as the ABSOLUTE hp (`stat_change`).
- Increase HP Recovery 10 ticks every 10 s by `5 x lv + MaxHP x lv / 500` (= 155). It is sent as
  ZC_RECOVERY 0x0A27 (`recovery`, decoded live since the 20:21 recreate).
- **While walking** (`ud->walktimer` set): skill regen (IRP) is OFF always (:15527). Natural regen
  continues only with Moving HP Recovery (`regen->state.walk`, :4653), at the doubled interval
  (12 s, :15550).
- Attacking and being hit change neither rule.
- Per minute: standing ≈ 330 + 930 = **1,260 HP/min**; walking ≈ **165 HP/min** (no IRP).

**The trial (`scripts/regen_walk.py`, the Crusader at prt_fild08 268,107; the box 258-278 x
102-112 passes `check_warps`: no warp span, no NPC touch area, server-walkable):**
- 2 cycles, each starting with `@killmonster2` and `@heal -3000` (atcommand.cpp:1398-1399:
  `status_damage`), so that HP stays under its max.
- Each cycle has three 60-s phases:
  - **S**, standing, no keys.
  - **W**, walking: alternating 7-cell walks east / west, clicked by pixels only: two-motion hover,
    WALK cursor read twice (`walk10.Prober9`, v3 refs), a direction flip only after a click.
  - **F**, standing while ONE Orc Zombie attacks, with S1b + S2 (the potion at 60 %).
- No Fly Wing, no Auto Guard.

**Measures (packets, offline):**
- recovery ticks (amount, count) and natural ticks (+33 steps of the hp series) per phase, each
  tick classed by whether we were walking at it (our `self_move` paths);
- HP/min regen per phase, against the predictions above.

**Positive cases:**
- the `recovery` decoder: >= 1 `recovery` hp event of 155 in an S phase (§2a's pending row);
- the walk rule: no IRP tick while walking.

**Safety:**
- every W click needs the WALK cursor twice, and is skipped otherwise;
- any `act` from us of kind `normal` in an S or W phase is a non-target hit: it stops the trial and
  is reported;
- the UI gate on every typed line; the name + job check before every GM line.

This is a measurement, not an adoption: no bar decides a version.

**Run log (`20261021T212245-demo-crusader-regen-r1`, 21:22:45-21:30:30; judged by `regen_walk.py
judge`, packets):**

| cycle / phase | minutes | walking share | IRP ticks (155) | of them while walking | natural ticks (33) | of them while walking | regen HP/min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 S | 1.01 | 0 | 6 | - | 10 | - | **1,234** |
| 0 W | 1.04 | 0.30 | 4 | **0** | 10 | 0 | 909 |
| 0 F | 1.01 | 0 | 3 (one capped at 5: HP met its max) | - | 5 | - | 470 (HP at max part of the phase) |
| 1 S | 1.02 | 0 | 6 | - | 10 | - | **1,231** |
| 1 W | 1.04 | 0.29 | 4 | **0** | 10 | 0 | 902 |
| 1 F | 1.01 | 0 | 5 | - | 8 | - | 1,023 |

- **Positive case, the `recovery` decoder: PASS.** 155-HP `recovery` events are decoded live (12
  in the S phases), so the §2a row is now PASS.
- **Standing:** 1,232 HP/min against the predicted 1,260.
- **The walk rule: IRP never ticked while walking** (0 of 8 IRP ticks in W). They accrued only in
  the standing gaps: 4 a minute at a 30 % walking share against 6 standing.
- **Fighting (one Orc Zombie on us):** regen continues. Both kinds of tick arrive while the
  monster hits. In cycle 0, HP reached its max, which stops skill regen.
- **NOT answered: natural regen WHILE moving (Moving HP Recovery's doubled interval).**
  - Every W click goes through the cursor gate (two reads), which costs about as long as the
    9-cell walk. So the walking share was only ~30 %, and every natural tick (20 of 20) fell in a
    standing gap.
  - With MHR the interval while walking is 12 s, but a 6-s standing gap always comes first, so
    walks shorter than 12 s cannot show it. This is a design limit, not evidence against MHR.
  - Seeing it needs > 12 s of continuous walking: a long route, or re-clicks in motion, where
    the cursor reads are unreliable ("cursor redraw lags in motion").
- **For the dungeon (Batt's question):**
  - At the bot's real rhythm (short walks between standing actions, here 30 % walking), regen is
    ~905 HP/min: ~74 % of standing.
  - Walking continuously, the source predicts ~165 HP/min, natural only (IRP is off).
  - So regen "keeps up" only through the standing and fighting time. A pack's burst (2,200-17,000
    HP/min in T-S2) is far above any regen: potions remain the real sustain.

**Batt's brief (abridged):**
- ENGAGEMENT WITHOUT A TRAINED DETECTOR: measure v1's zero-shot boxes on col1-col3 first. Then
  "DEFEND-SCAN": when the Battle Log shows "[X] inflicts ... on you", or HP drops, or a v1 box is
  near, hover the cells around the drawn GM (two motions) and on SWORD burst-click (arm C) until the
  lock arrow. The damage line's [name] gives the species. Search between fights with the heading
  walk. Warps: zones, delegated, proved.
- A REST SPOT: monster-free cells from col1-col3 packets; rest = sit until HP is full; if hit
  while sitting, stand and fight or escape.
- Verify from the pinned rAthena: Heal at Lv 8 (amount, SP), Heal on undead, sitting regen,
  potion and Fly Wing behaviour.
- A. POTIONS; B. REST; C. HEAL BUILD (Batt's skill tree). Runs ~45-60 min, alternated, as many
  as fit before ~18:30.
- Measures: kills/h, deaths/h, HP min, potions/h, Fly Wings/h, Heals/h and SP used, resting %,
  loot completeness, gross and NET zeny/h, cost ratio, Sharpe-like, Moving HP Recovery ticks while
  walking. Hard bars: map change, unknown UI state, NPC contact. A DEATH is a result.

4. **The pinned rAthena (e985006), verified in the source:**
   - Heal (pre-renewal `skill_calc_heal`): (BaseLv + INT) / 8 x (4 + 8 x Lv) = (60 + 7) / 8 =
     8 x 68 = **544 HP** at Lv 8 (Batt's ~470 is the same formula with INT 1: 61 / 8 = 7 x 68 =
     476; the Crusader's Job-50 bonus makes INT 7). **34 SP** (skill_db AL_HEAL), no cast time,
     1 s after-cast delay, range 9. MaxSP 312 = 9 Heals from full.
   - Heal on UNDEAD (battle.cpp `AL_HEAL`): `skill_calc_heal(..., heal=false)` = half, **272**,
     then the Holy-vs-Undead element table (Undead 1 = 150 %) and MDEF. Not used in these runs
     (Batt: "separate, not in the first C runs").
   - SITTING (status.cpp `status_natural_heal`): the natural HP and SP intervals are HALVED
     (`multi += 1`): 6 s -> 3 s for HP, 8 s -> 4 s for SP. Increase HP Recovery's 10-s tick is
     unchanged. So HP regen 1,250 -> ~1,570 HP/min (+26 %) and SP 37.5 -> 75 /min. No sitting skill
     regen for a Crusader (only Spirits Recovery / the Taekwon skills).
   - Being hit does NOT make a player stand; only a hit blocked by Auto Guard does (battle.cpp
     1536, `pc_setstand`). So "hit while sitting -> stand" is the runner's own press.
   - The skill reset (`pc_resetskill`) keeps Basic Skill and the quest skills
     (`quest_skill_reset: no`); `player_skillup_limit: yes` needs 9 + 49 points spent before any
     Crusader skill.
   - White Potion and Fly Wing: 3.96's (no per-item delay, `item_use_interval` 100 ms; a Fly Wing
     teleports to a random cell of the same map, which the client sees as a same-map map change).

     LIST kept across the fight (our cell at EVERY kill; the loot step covers the union of the

**The runner, `scripts/dungeon_hunt.py` (dungeon@2, code 129c459):**
- **Triggers** (each logged as `engage` with `by`): a Battle Log hit on us; the HP percent falling
  >= 2 points within 1.5 s; a v1 box whose foot is within 110 px of our cell's point (the detector
  at 1 Hz in its own thread, its own grab helper). And three more: a SWORD where a walk click was
  about to go (`walk_sword`), a SWORD in the loot hover (`loot_sword`), and the ring-1 scan after a
  walk stall (`stall_scan`). ONE `engage` event per fight, by what started it.
- **DEFEND-SCAN:** hover ring 1 (orthogonal first), then ring 2 (only while hits still come), at
  each cell's projected point 26 px up (the body); a kill with no hit for 2.5 s ends the fight at
  once (pilot 4); a SWORD -> strike there: click, re-click every 0.6 s until the client's
  lock arrow (searched 150..10 px above the point), at most 4 clicks / 3 s. Then wait for the kill
  (a Base EXP line); no hit of ours for 3.5 s -> scan again.
- **Sustain inside long actions:** the HP / SP are read between the hovers and between the burst
  clicks (`guard_tick`, at most every 0.25 s), with the strategy's keys.
- **LOOT (after the FIGHT, Batt's list):** the 5 x 5 around our cell at every kill of the fight,
  then the changed-cell sweep (item 9); click only on a PICKUP hand; a SWORD there is engaged.
- **SEARCH:** `hunt_flow.heading_goal` on the zone-free search area, A* on the zone-free route
  grid, a walk click every 1.2 s on the farthest path cell <= 7 ahead that is in view, off the UI
  and crosses no zone, only where the cursor reads clear and shows no red no-entry ring; two
  no-entry reads, or two clicks that do not move us, turn the heading (the stall also scans
  ring 1).
- **REST (B, C):** the nearest rest spot (Chebyshev), walked there by the same rule; Insert to
  sit; stand on HP 100 %, after 300 s, or on a hit (then fight).
- **Auto Guard:** 3.96's S4b2 in every strategy (F3 only when its icon is off).
- **Setup per run (the experimenter's restore):** at >= 40 % weight, `@warp` to the Crusader's
  prt_fild08 stand and drop the inventory's Etc tab (loot only; gm_state.clear_loot's known path);
  `@heal`; White Potions to 40 and Fly Wings to 15 by `@item` (counted from the DB's last save);
  the weight must read under 48 % (natural regen stops at 50 %, which would bias B and C);
  `@warp orcsdun01` to the seed's start cell.

**The strategies (the ONE thing that differs between A, B and C; `STRATEGIES` in the code):**

| | potion (F1) | Fly Wing (F2) | rest (sit until 100 %) | Heal (F5 + self) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A POTIONS | HP < 60 % (3.96's S2 pacing) | HP < 25 %, or > 200 HP/s while HP < 60 % | never | never |
| B REST | HP < 30 % (emergency) | HP < 20 %, or > 200 HP/s while HP < 40 % | after a fight with HP < 60 % | never |
| C HEAL | as B | as B | as B, only when SP < 11 % (34 SP) | HP < 60 % and SP >= 11 %, then every 1.1 s until 80 % |

**Runs:**
- 45 min each, orcsdun01, immunity OFF, a judged screenshot before each.
- Order: rounds of three, rotated so each strategy meets each slot of the afternoon:
  A B C, then B C A, then C A B, ... as many as fit before ~18:30 (the chain queues only 3.98's
  runs).
- Seeds: 22001, 22002, 22003, ... in run order (the start cell).
- A run stops early only on a hard bar or a death (a result, recorded with its cause); the next
  run follows.

**Measures (per run; pooled per strategy by `scripts/dungeon_judge.py table`):**
- From PACKETS: kills/h, deaths/h, HP min, potions/h, Fly Wings/h, Heals/h (an SP fall of exactly
  34, confirmed by +544 HP), SP used, Auto Guard casts, loot completeness (gross, net), gross and
  NET zeny/h at NPC prices (White Potion 1,200 z, Fly Wing 60 z, a Heal 0), cost ratio,
  Sharpe-like over 10-min windows, sitting %, Moving HP Recovery (natural ticks WHILE walking; IRP
  ticks while walking must be 0), hard bars.
- From EVENTS: resting %, engagements by trigger, strikes and their landing (a strike followed
  within 1.5 s by our attack request AND our act on a monster), escapes, the end reason.
- **Hard bars (stop the run):** a map change to ANOTHER map (a Fly Wing is a same-map teleport,
  counted apart), an NPC contact, an unknown UI state, an attack request on a non-monster.

**Predictions (written before the runs, for the record):**
- A: the most kills/h and the fewest deaths, at the highest cost (potions ~1,200 z each).
- B: the lowest cost and the highest resting %, fewer kills/h; deaths possible (emergency only).
- C: between them; Heals/h capped by SP regen (~37.5 SP/min standing = ~1.1 Heals/min, 75 sitting).
- Moving HP Recovery: natural ticks while walking at the doubled interval (~12 s), seen at last
  because the heading walk keeps moving for > 12 s at a time.

**Decision rule:** none; this is a COMPARISON for Batt (risk vs return), not an adoption.
- Fewer than 2 runs of a strategy: its numbers are single-run numbers, said so.
- A strategy with a death: its deaths/h is reported with the cause of each death (HP trace,
  attackers from the Battle Log and the packets).

### 3.99 dungeon@3-melee_ring: MELEE-RING engagement (the CURSOR engages, not the detector) vs 3.98's defend-scan, sustain B fixed, in alternating runs inside 3.98's rotation (pre-registered 2026-10-22 13:56 ICT, the commit time of 3.99's first commit, BEFORE its pilot and its runs; Batt 2026-10-22 ~13:4x: "NEW ENGAGE OPTION (Batt's idea): 'MELEE-RING' engagement, driven by the CURSOR, not the detector ... pre-register it as its own version on orcsdun01 with the Crusader, compared with the current detector/defend-scan engagement in alternating runs within today's A/B/C rotation (keep the sustain strategy fixed for this comparison, e.g. B)")

**Batt's behaviour, as built (`scripts/dungeon_hunt.py --engage melee_ring`, code c25f4c7):**
1. Searching, the walk legs are SHORT (3 cells ahead, not 7: "moving slowly"), and between the
   walk clicks the pointer rests on a ring-1 cell AHEAD of the walk (the step toward the next path
   cell and its two 45-degree neighbours, in turn; two-motion reads at the body point 26 px up).
   The moment the cursor reads SWORD there: strike (arm C: the click, re-clicks every 0.6 s until
   the lock arrow, <= 4 / 3 s). `engage` by `cursor`.
2. While LOCKED (swinging), ring 1 (the 8 cells around the drawn character, the locked one
   skipped) is re-read every 2 s by hovers only; every SWORD cell joins a QUEUE (once, by its
   absolute cell). On the kill (a Base EXP line) the next queued cell still beside us is re-read
   and, on SWORD, struck at once: no walking between them (`handoff`, with the ms from the kill).
   No queued SWORD left -> 3.98's ring scan, then the fight ends.
3. One loot step per fight: 3.98's loot LIST (the union of the 5 x 5 at every death of the
   fight) and its sweep over the cells changed since the fight began; PICKUP-hand clicks.
4. Then the search resumes (short legs + the forward watch) until the next pack.
- The Battle Log hit and the HP drop still START a fight (being hit while walking); the v1 box
  watcher is OFF (the detector is not the engagement source here).
- Everything else is 3.98's dungeon@2 at the same code: sustain B (potion / Fly Wing emergencies,
  the rest at a rest spot), Auto Guard, zones, the no-entry veto, the stall / idle / Fly Wing
  fixes (Amendments C-F), FrameGuard. NPCs read TALK, never SWORD (orcsdun01 has none anyway).

cancel or retarget the attack; if it does, scan only between swings or after the lock".

  every hover window while locked from the packets: `kept` (our next act is on the same target),

**The two arms (everything else identical; `scripts/dungeon_hunt.py`, dungeon@4, code e8273db + the
`map_routes` loader merged before the pilot):**
- **P (patrol):** `--search patrol` -- walk `batt-loop`'s waypoints in their listed order; join at
  the nearest waypoint ahead (`map_routes.entry_index`) at the start and after a Fly Wing; a fight,
  a loot step or a rest interrupts the loop, and the walk resumes at the NEXT waypoint AHEAD
  (`map_routes.resume_index`: never a passed one); a waypoint counts as reached within 2 cells; one
  that does not route (carved) is skipped forward.
- **C (control, "the current search"):** `--search heading` -- 3.98's heading walk.
- **The BASE both share (dungeon@4; Batt's decisions on the 19:00 report):**
  - sustain **H = B + Heal** (decision 1, and his demo's rhythm): in a fight Heal below 50 % HP
    while SP pays; between fights (no hit for 2 s) Heal below 93 % with SP >= 85 %; potions only
    in an emergency (below 30 %); the Fly Wing escape as B (below 20 %, or > 200 HP/s under 40 %);
  - **rest** after a fight when HP < 80 % or SP < 30 % (decision 1b), sitting until HP >= 99 % and
    SP >= 40 % (<= 300 s); then back INTO the search area (the heading arm walks to the nearest
    area cell first) or onto the route (the patrol arm re-joins it);
  - decision 5's fixes: the strike's burst ENDS on our first damage line in the Battle Log, and a
    walk target the cursor reads NO-ENTRY is carved off the route grid at once;
  - **White Plants** (Batt: killed on purpose for the White Herb): passing within 7 cells of a White
    Plant spawn area (83,50 +-5; 58,67 +-10; rAthena's spawn lines), the cursor sweeps its nearest
    cells on a 2-cell lattice (<= 16 hovers; each area at most every 120 s); a SWORD there is struck

### 4.01 dungeon@4 + LOOT v2: the changed cells first, a time budget per fight, no re-hover of empty cells, vs dungeon@4's loot (pre-registered 2026-10-22, the commit time of 4.01's first commit, BEFORE its code is merged or run; Batt's decision 4 on the 19:00 report: "Loot: hover the CHANGED cells first, the plain list cells after; a time budget per fight; skip cells already hovered empty"; his overnight brief: "Then, if time remains, the loot change (item 4) as its own version")

**Why:** Batt's demo vs the bot (crusader-orcsdun01.md 9a): the bot's largest gap is STANDING
between fights, 24.8 s / kill (3.98 defend), of which its loot step ~10.7 s / kill (each step up
to 25 s and 30 hovers); 83 of Batt's 88 pickups came within 10 s after a fight.

**The change (`--loot v2`, code 271ece3 on feat/loot-v2, rebased on Amendment I; merged into main
only after 4.00's chain ends, so 4.00's runs keep their code) -- ➡️ MERGED 2026-10-23 05:36 ICT
(e28272f), after 4.00's last run; NOT run yet (no client time remained before the 07:00 end state):**
1. **Changed cells first:** at the step's start, every in-view cell whose image changed since the
   fight began (3.98's sweep rule: a 24 x 20 grey patch, mean |diff| >= 15) is hovered first,
   nearest first; then the plain loot-list cells (the 5 x 5 around each kill of the fight), nearest
   first, once each.
2. **One time budget per FIGHT: 10 s,** shared by every loot step after the same fight (a step
   interrupted by a new fight resumes with what is left).
3. **No re-hover of an empty cell:** a cell hovered with no PICKUP hand is skipped for the rest of
   the fight series, unless a kill came within 2 cells of it AFTER that hover.
4. Bounds: <= 10 picks, <= 40 hovers a step. PICKUP -> click, SWORD -> fight, as today.

**Arms (paired, alternating; everything else 4.00's base after Amendment I):** L2 = `--loot v2`,
L1 = dungeon@4's loot (v1). The SEARCH both use is the one 4.00 favours at the time of the first
4.01 run (patrol if 4.00's pairs favour it, else heading), said in the run log before run 1.
**An unscored pilot (L2, ~5 min) first;** a bug = an amendment before run 1.

**Measures (per run, pooled per arm):** the loot step's seconds per kill (events) and standing
outside fights per kill (`dungeon_style.py`); loot completeness gross / net and the fates
(`loot_complete`: picked, looters, expired, out of sight); items per pick hover; kills / h; net
zeny / h; HP min; deaths.

**Expectation (stated before any run), no adoption rule tonight:** L2 spends less loot time per
kill than L1 and loses at most 5 points of gross completeness. The decision is Batt's.

its time). Batt's decisions on the overnight report (received ~22:1x ICT), verbatim:**

**What changes (the BASE of BOTH arms, `dungeon@5`; nothing else in 4.01 changes):**
- **The search:** `--search patrol` for L1 and L2 (4.01's own rule already named the search 4.00
  favours; Batt adopted it).
- **Decision 6, no plant sweep:** `--plant-sweep` is off. A White Plant is struck only when the run
  meets it as any monster: a SWORD read by a walk click's cursor check, a loot hover or a defend
  scan.
- **Decision 4, box spots:** a box-started fight that ends with NO strike is a MISS at the box's
  spot (the map cell under the box's foot: the camera's projection grid, the nearest cell). Once
  the misses within 1 cell (Chebyshev; the foot jitters) reach 2, the box trigger passes over boxes
  there for the rest of the run (a monster that hits us still starts a fight by the Battle Log or
  the HP drop). Events: `box_miss`, `box_ignored` (rate-limited), `box_watch.spots_ignored`.
  - Its real case (a test, `test_dungeon5_a_box_spot_is_ignored_after_two_box_fights_without_a_sword`):

    Black Mushroom spawn.

**Amendment B (2026-10-23 ~22:4x ICT, after the pilot, BEFORE run 1; the parent):**
- **The cause:** `patch()` (a cell's 24 x 20 grey patch) converted the WHOLE frame to grey on every
  call: ~44 ms a call on tonight's loaded CPU (measured), two calls per cell, ~200 cells in view.
- **The same code runs in v1's sweep** (after its list): 4.00's pi6 loot steps that ended "done"
  took p50 23.4 s for p50 29.5 hovers (34 steps) -- a part of 4.00's "standing" was this
  computation, in BOTH 4.00 arms.
- **The fix (both arms, the same cells and diffs):** each frame goes grey ONCE per changed-cell
  computation and the cells are projected in one batch (`grey()`, `changed_cells(ref, skip=)`;
  v1's sweep now calls the same helper with its list's hovered cells as `skip`).
- It changes how fast both loot steps run, not what they choose. L1 is therefore faster than 4.00's
  P arm; the pairs compare L1 and L2 under the same fix.

- **The expectation held only in part.** L2 spends less loot time per kill (3.19 vs 7.77 s), but it
  lost **38 points** of gross completeness, not "at most 5". Its items went to LOOTERS: in li1, 79
  of 237 items, against 12 of 79 in ll1. A 10-s budget plus "no re-hover of empty cells" leaves
  items behind, and in a dense spell the looters take them.

  against four starved runs (met 15-22). The population along the loop collapsed through the
  night (Orc Zombies seen per run 49 -> 12 -> 2; see 4.02 Amendment A). Pairs 2 and 3 say little
  about loot.
- **Amendment B's fix lowered L1's loot time too** (v1 steps p50 11.8 s, against 23.4 s in 4.00),
  so L1 here is not 4.00's P arm.
- **For Batt:** loot v2 trades completeness for time. Batt's own rhythm (4.02) bounds the time
  harder and relies on the loop to come back for the rest.

**Decision 7's packet check (offline, 2026-10-23 23:0x ICT; no runner change):** "the 160 'no icon
while remembered' cases: check the status packets".
- **How:** a new decoder for the status icons, ZC_MSG_STATE_CHANGE 0x0196 / 0x0983 (`status_change`:
  the icon id, the block, on / off, the timers; Auto Guard = EFST 58). It is on branch
  `feat/status-change` (c62a6de); the ids are not in the lock's disagreements, so the table and lock
  are unchanged.
  - 4.00's captures (2026-10-22 13-22 UTC, 11 files) were replayed with it
    (`guarded_build.py replaydev:`, 74 s, worst capture stall 6.0 %): 88,149 events, 172 Auto Guard
    packets for the Crusader (86 on, 86 off).
  - The 387 diagnostic frames were joined with the server's state at their time.
- **The 227 frames the dungeon bar reads PRESENT: the server said ON for all 227.** The field bar
  (30) had misread every one.
- **The 160 frames read ABSENT:**
  - 143: the server said OFF, and Auto Guard had EXPIRED at its 300 s each time;
  - 17: the server said ON but the client drew NO status icon (scores 68-175; e.g. pi4 #10 under
    Blind's dark vignette, pi5 #5 with an empty status column in a normal scene).
- **Uptime:** Auto Guard was up **76.6 %** of the 13 runs' time (per run 48-98 %).
  - All 80 off packets inside the runs were 300-s expiries; NONE was our F3 toggling it off.
  - **15 expiries were followed by more than 200 s without it**: the runner recasts only 300 s after
    its REMEMBERED cast, and that memory can run late (S4b2: an icon first seen on counts as "just
    cast").
- **For Batt (a later version, not tonight's base):** with the dungeon bar's presence now matching
  the server on 227 / 227 frames, recast as soon as the icon has read absent for a few seconds on a
  scene that is not dark, instead of waiting for 300 s after the remembered cast. The 17 frames
  with no icon while it was on are that rule's toggle-off risk; they need a wider "dark / no icons"
  guard (e.g. no other status icon in the column either).

### 4.02 dungeon@5 + LOOT RHYTHM: Batt's demo rhythm -- 1-2 pickups, move on within ~2.5 s, the loop recovers the rest -- vs the patrol base's loot, in PAIRED runs (pre-registered 2026-10-23, the commit time of 4.02's first commit, BEFORE its code is built or run; Batt's decision 2 on the overnight report, received ~22:1x ICT: "Then, as its own next version, Batt's real loot rhythm from his demo: click what is seen/found quickly (1-2 pickups), move on within ~2-3 s, and let the loop recover the rest (his gross 68 % -> net 95.7 %: looters' items come back when he kills them on the next lap). Measure gross AND net completeness, s per kill, standing time, monsters pulled along.")

**Why (Batt's demo, 4.00's source):** he moved on 2.4 s after a fight (median) with one pickup; 83
of his 88 pickups came within 10 s after a fight; gross 68.2 % / net 95.7 % (looters took 40, 37
re-dropped when he killed them). The bot's loot step took 722-965 s of every 40-min 4.00 run
(30-40 %), the largest part of its standing time (P: 9.6 s / kill standing vs his 1.6).

**The change (`--loot rhythm`, dungeon@5's base otherwise):** loot v2's ORDER (4.01: the cells
whose image changed since the fight began first, then the 5 x 5 list cells around the fight's
kills, nearest first; a cell hovered empty is not hovered again unless a kill came near it
after), with Batt's rhythm as its bounds:
- **one time budget per FIGHT: 2.5 s** (v2: 10 s), shared by every loot step after the same
  fight, checked before each hover (a pickup click already made completes its walk);
- **at most 2 pickups per fight** (v2: 10);
- PICKUP -> click, SWORD -> fight, as v1 / v2. Nothing else changes; the patrol loop "recovers
  the rest" by passing again.

**Arms (paired, alternating; everything else dungeon@5 on the patrol loop):** R = `--loot rhythm`,
L1 = `--loot v1` (the patrol base's loot: 4.01's control, so 4.01's L2 and 4.02's R are each set
against the same base). **An unscored R pilot (~5 min) first;** a bug = an amendment before run 1.

**Runs:** after 4.01's three pairs (4.01 Amendment A), 40 min each, R first in odd pairs, L1 first in
even pairs (labels ri1 / rl1, rl2 / ri2, ...; seeds 23301, 23302, ...); as many pairs as fit, the
last run ending its time box by ~06:30 ICT; a pair is complete only with both runs full.

**Measures (per run, pooled per arm; `dungeon_judge.py` + `dungeon_style.py` + `loot_complete`,
packets):** loot completeness GROSS and NET and the fates (picked, looters, re-dropped, expired,
out of sight); the loot step's seconds per kill; seconds per kill split fighting / walking /
STANDING outside fights; monsters PULLED ALONG / 10 min; kills / h; monsters met / 10 min; net
zeny / h; HP min; potions, Fly Wings, Heals; deaths; hard bars. Batt's demo beside them (target).

**Expectation (stated before any run), no adoption rule:** R spends less loot time and less
standing time per kill than L1 and kills more per hour; its GROSS completeness is lower than L1's;
its NET completeness is within 10 points of L1's. The decision is Batt's.

**Hard bars and deaths:** as 4.00 / 4.01.
